## 2026-07-18 — Needs-Attention card reappeared after approval + no outcome visibility
**What happened (Scott, direct report):** approved a Conversion Doctor fix for the "Dinosaur Coloring Book" listing (377 views, 0 sales). The identical Needs-Attention card was back the instant the action left "pending," and there was no way to tell whether the fix actually landed on Etsy.

**Root cause 1 -- card reappearing.** The `low_conversion` rule (and its siblings `title_too_long`/`tags_incomplete`/`zero_views`) fires purely off live `views`/`sales`/`title`/`tags` from Etsy. The only fix types the Conversion Doctor can stage (`update_title`/`update_tags`/`update_description`) edit content, never those metrics. A pending-only exclusion filter shipped earlier today only covered the staging-to-approval window; the instant the row left "pending" the card recomputed against still-unchanged metrics and came right back. Per this repo's own Ranking Recovery Playbook, Etsy takes ~2-3 weeks to re-index an edited listing before those numbers can move at all -- no fix, however successful, could make this card disappear same-day.

**Fix 1:** `_compute_actions()` (`tools/api_server/main.py`) now reuses the edit-cooldown timestamp `db.note_listing_edited()` already records (built 2026-07-15 for a different purpose -- warning against compounding edits inside the ranking-recovery window) via a new `db.days_since_listing_edited()`. Any of the four content-fixable categories, for a listing edited within `db._RANKING_RECOVERY_COOLDOWN_DAYS` (21d), gets its severity downgraded to `low` and its suggestion rewritten to confirm the fix and explain the wait, instead of silently reappearing unchanged. The card stays visible rather than vanishing -- an invisible card gave zero confirmation, which was the other half of the report.

**Root cause 2 -- no outcome visibility.** `POST /api/queue/{id}/approve` already returned the real Etsy response in `result`, and `GET /api/queue?status=all` already existed server-side, but nothing in the frontend ever used either: `approveAction()` was silent on success, and both the mobile Approvals panel and desktop Action Center only ever fetched `status=pending` -- the moment an action left "pending," it vanished with no trace, success or failure.

**Fix 2:** `approveAction()` (`tools/api_server/frank_hud_mockup.py`) now shows a success toast built from the real result (e.g. "✅ title updated: \"New Fixed Title\""). New shared `_recentActivityHtml()` renders a "Recently completed" list (last 5 non-pending actions, ✅/❌ + outcome text) in both the mobile Approvals panel (`renderPhoneApprovals()`) and desktop Action Center (`loadActions()`/`renderActionsContent()`), reusing the already-existing `status=all` endpoint.

**Playwright gotcha hit while testing this:** the app registers a service worker (`frank-sw.js`) whose `fetch` handler intercepts every GET via its own internal `fetch(req)` call -- that fetch happens inside the SW's execution context, which `page.route()` does not see by default. A mocked `/api/queue?status=all` route was silently never hit; the real (empty, local-DB) backend response came through instead, with the mock router registered correctly and matching by every other diagnostic. Fix: test the shared render function (`_recentActivityHtml()`) directly with synthetic data instead of mocking the network call, same as the existing `_products`/`_listings` fixture pattern already used elsewhere in `playwright_smoke.py` for exactly this reason.

**Tests:** `tests/test_needs_attention_pending_filter.py` extended (5 new cases: recently-edited card downgraded not hidden, edit outside the cooldown window is untouched, never-edited is untouched, a non-content-fixable category like `draft_unpublished` is never downgraded even with a recent edit timestamp for that listing, and `days_since_listing_edited` round-trips through `note_listing_edited` including a malformed-timestamp fallback to `None`). `playwright_smoke.py` extended with a direct `_recentActivityHtml()` check (empty list renders nothing, a filled list shows the right icons/outcome text for both executed and failed actions).

## 2026-07-18 — 5 animations/graphics implemented from the design-research pass
**What (Scott, from the design-research artifact):** "See if there are any animations or graphics that we should implement into Frank."

All 5 ranked recommendations from the research artifact, implemented in `tools/api_server/frank_hud_mockup.py`:

1. **Skeleton loaders** — new `_skeletonCards(n, kind)` helper (content-shaped shimmer, `.skel-card`/`.skel-tile`/`.skel-bar` CSS, respects `prefers-reduced-motion`). Wired into the highest-traffic loading states: Today tab tiles+cards (`renderPhoneToday`, first load only — see #3), Products (`loadProducts`), Approvals mobile (`renderPhoneApprovals`) and desktop (`loadActions`).
2. **Count-up stat tiles** — new `_animateCountUp(el, targetText)` (~260ms ease-out cubic, `requestAnimationFrame`-driven, handles plain integers and `$123.45`-style currency, falls straight to the final value for non-numeric text like `show()`'s `—` placeholder or under `prefers-reduced-motion`). Wired into Today's Orders/Rev/Sales tiles; `.ptile .n` gained `font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums` so digits don't jitter horizontally mid-animation.
3. **Card-resolve animation** — a Needs-Attention card that drops out between renders (Frank fixed it, or it genuinely cleared) now visibly collapses (`.palert.resolving`, `@keyframes need-resolve`, ~420ms) instead of vanishing on the next re-render. `renderPhoneToday()` now tracks `_phoneNeedsKeys` (a stable per-card key: `l:{listing_id}` or `a:{title}`) across renders, diffs old vs. new, and only shows the skeleton loader on a genuine first load (`el.dataset.loadedOnce`) — a refresh resolves smoothly instead of flashing back to a loading state.
4. **Success checkmark on approve** — `showToast(message, 'ok', ms)` now draws a real animated checkmark (`.toast-check`, spring pop-in via `cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1)`) instead of relying on an emoji character. `approveAction()`'s redundant `'✅ '` text prefix removed since the icon now carries that signal.
5. **Star Seller milestone badge** — `renderPhoneToday()` now also fetches `/api/star-seller` (already existed, just never surfaced on Today) and shows a small gold-glow `.pmilestone` badge when `status === 'on_track'` (real orders_90d/revenue_90d/avg_rating), per the research's "rare, genuinely earned moments deserve more personality than constant-frequency UI" finding.

**New/extended tests:** `playwright_smoke.py` — `_skeletonCards()` pure-function output check; Today-tab first-load + resolve-animation test (stubs `authGet` directly rather than mocking network, same seam used for `_recentActivityHtml` below — the app's service worker intercepts every GET via its own internal `fetch()`, invisible to `page.route()`, but does NOT intercept POST (`frank-sw.js`'s fetch handler returns early on non-GET), confirmed by successfully mocking the `/api/queue/{id}/approve` POST for the checkmark test); count-up settles on the exact real value with no float drift; milestone badge renders with real numbers when `on_track`; success toast shows the animated checkmark SVG. ## 2026-07-18 — The orb replaced with a rotating 3D "OnBrandCraftz" wireframe wordmark (v224)

**Ask:** Scott: replace the noise-displaced icosahedron ("the orb") on the mobile Ask
tab / desktop landing view with a slowly-rotating 3D rendering of the shop name,
wireframe letters, matching whichever font pairing is active in Settings, with the
"Frank / SHOP ASSISTANT" text overlay dropped in favor of the wordmark itself. Some
speech-reactivity kept, but as "a soft glow reactive to speech" rather than the
sphere's turbulence.

**Approach:** the string never changes ("OnBrandCraftz"), so instead of vendoring a
full FontLoader/TextGeometry pipeline, 5 outline SVGs (one per font pairing:
Fraunces/Playfair Display/Space Grotesk/Fredoka/Sora) were pre-generated offline via
fontTools + HarfBuzz (real glyph shaping/kerning, viewBox sized from the actual shaped
bounding box) and saved under `static/vendor/wordmark/onbrandcraftz-{pairing}.svg`.
Three.js's `SVGLoader` (newly vendored, matching the existing r160 build) loads the
matching SVG at runtime and `ExtrudeGeometry` gives each letter real 3D depth;
`initOrbGL()` swaps `IcosahedronGeometry` for this, `orbGLFrame()` drops the noise
vertex-displacement shader (rigid letters can't wobble) and keeps only Y-axis rotation,
constant speed, no amp-driven speed-up. `_ORB_VERT` is now a plain passthrough — the
old `_ORB_NOISE_GLSL` simplex-noise function is gone, not needed by any current shader.

**Two real bugs caught during verification (both fixed before shipping):**

1. **TDZ `ReferenceError` on every page load.** `_setFontPairing()` (Settings) was
   wired to call the new async `_rebuildWordmarkForPairing()` so switching pairings
   rebuilds the wordmark's typeface. But `_setFontPairing()` also runs immediately at
   module-parse time via its own startup IIFE (`_setFontPairing(_getFontPairing())`),
   which executes *before* the `let orbGLReady = ...` declaration further down the same
   script — accessing a `let` binding before its declaration line runs is a temporal
   dead zone violation. Caught by `tools/playwright_smoke.py`'s console-error check:
   `pageerror: Cannot access 'orbGLReady' before initialization`, twice. Because
   `_rebuildWordmarkForPairing` is `async`, the TDZ throw inside its body doesn't
   propagate as a synchronous exception to the caller (async functions convert even
   their own synchronous-portion throws into a rejected promise) — a plain
   `try/catch` around the call site would NOT have caught it. Fix: call
   `_rebuildWordmarkForPairing(p.name).catch(function(){})` instead of the
   `typeof === 'function'` guard alone. On the very first (startup) call this
   harmlessly no-ops (nothing to rebuild yet); every real user-driven pairing change
   from the Settings swatches runs long after `orbGLReady` is a real, initialized
   binding, so it always resolves normally there.

2. **Wordmark invisible — geometry built in raw font-design-space units, silently
   clipped by the camera's far plane.** The authored SVGs' path coordinates are direct
   font-outline units (upm ~1000–2000, so "OnBrandCraftz" is ~13,700 units wide for the
   default Fraunces pairing) — `ExtrudeGeometry` inherits those same huge units.
   `initOrbGL()`'s dynamic camera-fit calculation (distance derived from the actual
   built geometry's bounding box, replacing the sphere's fixed `z=6.5`) correctly
   computed a distance to fit that huge box in frame — but the result was `z≈24,142`,
   while the `PerspectiveCamera`'s far-clip plane (tuned for the old icosahedron's
   ~1.15-unit radius) was only `100`. The entire mesh sat far beyond the far plane and
   was silently clipped — the canvas rendered a real WebGL frame, `orbGLReady` was
   `true`, `glMesh.children.length` was correct (21, matching 13 shaped glyphs with a
   few multi-part letters), but a raw pixel-alpha sample of the canvas came back 100%
   transparent. Caught by manually screenshotting `#orb-view` and finding it visually
   blank, then instrumenting `page.evaluate()` to read `glCamera.position.z` and
   `glMesh.userData.fitSize` directly — the huge numbers immediately pointed at scale,
   not a logic bug in the shader/material/mesh-construction code (all of which were
   otherwise correct). Fix: every loaded geometry is now uniformly scaled (baked into
   its own vertex data via `geo.scale(scale, -scale, scale)`, combined with the
   existing SVG-to-Three.js Y-flip in the same call) so the wordmark's own height
   normalizes to a fixed small constant (`_WORDMARK_TARGET_HEIGHT = 1.6`) regardless of
   source font size — camera-fit distance is computed from the *already-scaled*
   geometry, so the absolute target value doesn't matter, only that vertex coordinates
   land back in "a few units," matching the near/far planes and the rest of the scene's
   existing unit convention. Post-fix: `camZ≈22.7`, comfortably inside `(0.1, 100)`.

**Verify:** `python -m py_compile`; inline `<script>` extracted from the real
(business_config-substituted) `_FRANK_HUD_MOCKUP` string and `node --check`'d (a naive
regex-extract of the raw file source falsely flagged pre-existing, correct
`\\'`-in-Python-source JS-escaping as a syntax error — had to actually import the
module and read the runtime string value instead); full `tests/run_all.py` (41/41,
including the pre-existing `test_frank_font_pairings.py`); `tools/check_hardcoded_paths.py`
clean; `tools/playwright_smoke.py` green across 5 consecutive runs post-fix (one flake
caught and fixed mid-session was the TDZ bug above — not reproduced in 2 later manual
Playwright repros of the same tour-click sequence, consistent with it being the
now-fixed root cause rather than an unrelated intermittent flake); manual Playwright
screenshots of `#orb-view` confirmed the wordmark renders correctly, centered, no
clipping, in all 5 font pairings (Fraunces/Playfair Display/Space Grotesk/Fredoka/Sora)
at both a 1440×1000 desktop viewport and a 390×844 mobile viewport, with the "Frank /
SHOP ASSISTANT" overlay text gone and the tiny build-version diagnostic line (`.o3`,
hidden by default behind the `show-plumbing` dev flag) relocated below the hero stage
instead of overlaid on top of it. `_BUILD_ID` bumped v223→v224.

**Also fixed in passing, same session, upstream of this feature:**
`fonts/PlayfairDisplay-Bold.ttf` was discovered corrupted (`file` identified it as an
HTML document, not a real TTF — `fontTools.ttLib.TTLibError: Not a TrueType or OpenType
font (bad sfntVersion)` when the SVG-authoring script tried to load it) while sourcing
raw font files for the 5 wordmark SVGs. Overwritten with a real Playfair Display Bold
TTF (instantiated wght=700 from Google Fonts' variable-font source). Note:
`fonts/PlayfairDisplay-Italic.ttf` in the same directory has the identical corruption
and was NOT fixed — nothing currently uses it, flagging here in case that changes.

**Lesson for next time:** when porting geometry from a real-world unit system (font
design units, GIS coordinates, CAD units, anything with its own native scale) into a
Three.js scene that already has an established "small numbers" convention (camera
near/far, existing meshes, bloom/glow tuning all implicitly assume a few units), always
explicitly normalize scale at the geometry-construction boundary — don't assume a
dynamic camera-fit calculation alone will compensate, since it can produce a distance
that's mathematically correct for framing but numerically outside the render pipeline's
clip range, failing completely silently (no error, no console warning, a real frame
renders, just with nothing non-transparent in it).

## 2026-07-18 — Wordmark stops rotating after switching mobile tabs and back (v225)

**Symptom (Scott):** "The words stop rotating when I switch tabs then go back. Find
the bug or glitch causing this. I need it fixed 100%." — the new 3D "OnBrandCraftz"
wordmark (v224, replacing the orb) would freeze/crawl for a beat after leaving the
mobile Ask tab (any of Approvals/Today/Create/More) and returning to it.

**Root cause, found by instrumented Playwright reproduction (not guessed):**
`orbGLFrame()` originally advanced rotation with a fixed **per-rAF-tick** constant
(`glMesh.rotation.y += 0.0022`). `#orb-view` is `display:none` on mobile whenever the
Ask tab isn't the active bottom-nav tab (`body.is-mobile #orb-view{display:none}`,
overridden only by `body.is-mobile.frank-popup-open`) — and browsers throttle
`requestAnimationFrame` for a page/canvas that isn't actually being painted, then only
ramp the tick rate back up gradually once it's visible again rather than resuming at
60fps instantly. A logged reproduction (`page.evaluate()` sampling `glMesh.rotation.y`,
`orbGLReady`, `orbGLPaused`, `document.hidden`, `cc-open` every 100ms across a real
`phoneTab('appr')` → wait → `phoneTab('ask')` cycle) confirmed: no WebGL context loss
occurred (the context-lost/restored console messages never fired, `orbGLReady` stayed
`true` throughout), all of `orbGLFrame()`'s own early-return guards stayed permissive
the whole time -- the rAF loop itself was just ticking far less often, so the
fixed-per-tick increment produced far less visible rotation per real second, reading
as "stopped."

**First attempt (partial fix, superseded):** switched to a delta-time
*accumulator* (`glClock.getDelta()`-style, matching how the old sphere's `uTime`
uniform worked) -- `rotation.y += dt * SPEED`. This is the standard pattern and
correctly fixed the "throttled-but-still-ticking" case (verified: rotation advanced
smoothly and proportionally to real elapsed time even while `#orb-view` was hidden).
But a longer instrumented run (rAF-tick counting, not a separate `setInterval` which
could itself be independently throttled) caught a SECOND, larger effect: right around
the moment `#orb-view` becomes visible again, `requestAnimationFrame` itself can stall
for several real *seconds* (7.3s observed in one capture) with no WebGL context loss
involved -- and whatever ticks DID fire during that stall didn't sum their individual
deltas back up to the true elapsed wall-clock time (only ~0.1 rad of the expected
~0.97 rad was recovered over that 7.3s gap). An accumulator can only ever add up what
each tick individually reports, so if the browser's own bookkeeping during a stall
under-reports elapsed time to individual ticks, the accumulator inherits that error
and the mesh still visibly lagged/crept for a beat after returning to the tab.

**Actual fix (shipped):** stopped accumulating altogether. `glStartTime =
performance.now()` is captured once in `initOrbGL()`; every frame, `orbGLFrame()`
computes rotation as a pure function of absolute elapsed time: `glMesh.rotation.y =
(elapsedSec * 0.132) % (2*PI)`. This has no accumulator to fall behind in the first
place -- whenever a frame finally does render, no matter how long the gap or how many
ticks were skipped or under-reported, it snaps to the mathematically correct CURRENT
angle immediately, with zero dependency on how reliably intermediate ticks fired.
`_rebuildWordmarkForPairing()` (font-pairing swap) no longer needs to copy the old
mesh's rotation onto the new one for the same reason -- the very next tick recomputes
it correctly regardless of what the new mesh starts at.

**Verify:** direct instrumented Playwright check across 4 repeated
Approvals→Ask cycles: sampled `glMesh.rotation.y` immediately on returning to the Ask
tab and again 400ms later, comparing against the deterministic formula
`(elapsedSec*0.132) % (2*PI)` computed independently in the same `page.evaluate()`
call. Immediately-on-return showed the expected small lag (up to ~0.9 rad in later
cycles, since no new frame had painted at that exact microsecond -- the canvas still
shows whatever the LAST frame before hiding rendered); 400ms later the lag closed to
~0.01–0.02 rad (one frame's worth of rounding), confirming the very next render call
snaps to the correct angle rather than crawling toward it. `python -m py_compile`;
inline `<script>` extracted from the real (business_config-substituted)
`_FRANK_HUD_MOCKUP` runtime string and `node --check`'d clean; full `tests/run_all.py`
(41/41); `tools/check_hardcoded_paths.py` clean; `tools/playwright_smoke.py` green
across 3 consecutive runs (one earlier run hit the same "Failed to fetch" wordmark-SVG
console error already documented as sandbox-environment flakiness in the v224 entry
above -- reran clean twice more, consistent with that being unrelated to this fix, not
a regression). `_BUILD_ID` bumped v224→v225.

**Lesson for next time:** don't assume "switch to delta-time" alone makes an animation
loop robust to throttling/backgrounding -- an accumulator is only as reliable as every
individual tick's delta being correctly reported, and a real browser CAN under-report
or entirely skip reporting elapsed time across a stall (observed directly, not
theoretical). Computing the animated value as a pure function of absolute wall-clock
time from a fixed reference point removes the accumulator entirely, so there's no
state that can fall behind or need to "catch up" -- it's correct at every instant
independent of tick history. This is a strictly stronger pattern than
delta-accumulation for any looping/periodic animation (rotation, pulsing, etc.) where
the exact path between two points in time doesn't matter, only the current value does.

## 2026-07-18 — Implemented the "Frank Against the Field" audit report's findings (v226)

**Ask:** Scott, after reviewing the competitive-research audit artifact: "Start at the
top and implement all that you can." Worked through the report's priority fix and its
"Ideas worth stealing" table in order, researching each against the real codebase
before building (2 background Explore agents + direct grep/read for a 3rd that hit a
session limit) rather than assuming the report's narrative examples were still
accurate — one of them (bundle-opportunity nudge) wasn't; see below.

**One real course correction, decided with Scott before building:** the report's
"confidence-tiered auto-apply" idea (let low-risk fixes skip the approval queue) would
have broken the Approvals screen's own stated promise, "nothing goes live without your
tap," and research found the batch-limit safety rail (10 edits / 5 price changes) is
frontend-only today, not server-enforced. Scott confirmed: ship a one-tap bulk-approve
convenience instead of a real skip-the-queue mechanism — see Phase 6 below. True
auto-apply and the report's "dry-run simulation" idea (needs a held-out case store +
scoring harness that don't exist yet) are both explicitly out of scope for this pass.

**Phase 1 — ops runbook dedup (the report's own priority fix).** Confirmed the root
cause by reading the code directly: every health-loop failure path funnels through
`_append_ops_runbook_entry()` (main.py) with zero dedup, which is exactly how one
issue ("No shop ID configured") produced 428 byte-identical entries. Added a same-day/
same-heading dedup guard (reads only the file's tail, ~4KB, to stay cheap on a hot
path) — genuine day-over-day recurrence still surfaces via the existing
`_promote_recurring_failures()` "Known Recurring Issues" summary, this only kills
same-day spam. Also ran a one-time cleanup of the already-bloated committed file:
15,497 lines / ~1MB collapsed to ~9,500 lines, with all 664 removed duplicate
occurrences archived in full (nothing deleted, per the standing "nothing we delete
should be unrecoverable" rule) to
`data/knowledge_base/_archive/ops_runbook_duplicates_2026-07-18.md`. New test:
`tests/test_ops_runbook_dedup.py`.

**Phase 2 — separated infra alerts from content-quality approvals.** Discovered
`_compute_actions()` already tags every scan card with a `category` field (infra
fetch failures use `"data_error"`) — the discriminator already existed, this was a
rendering split, not a new data model. `renderActionsContent()` now shows a "System
health" section separate from "Flagged by scan," and the severity-bucket counts are
recomputed from content-only cards so they no longer silently include an infra card's
severity.

**Phase 3 — "why Frank suggested this" reasoning panel.** Found
`_apply_conversion_fixes_core()` already computes a real `"finding → fix"` reason
string per autofix and threads it into the three autofix handlers as a `reason`
kwarg — but every handler discarded it after using it to steer the LLM prompt, so it
never reached the staged action's payload or the Approvals screen. Now
`payload["reason"]` is set (when non-empty) in all three handlers; the Gate 6
wall-art description path always has a reason even with none given, since it fires on
a deterministic rule. `_actionPreviewHtml()` split into a thin wrapper +
`_actionPreviewBody()` so a reason block renders uniformly across all action types
without touching each type's existing preview logic. New test:
`tests/test_action_reasoning_panel.py`.

**Phase 4 — reviews-needing-reply radar.** Confirmed Etsy's v3 API has no seller-reply
field on a review and no review-response endpoint at all (already documented in
`EtsyAPIClient.get_reviews()`'s own docstring) — "replied" can't come from Etsy, so
it's tracked locally in `data/reviews_replied.json` (gitignored, same buyer-adjacent-
content treatment as the existing `reviews_seen.json`), keyed by `transaction_id`
since a review has no dedicated review_id but is 1:1 with its transaction. New
`POST /api/reviews/{id}/mark-replied` endpoint; `/api/inbox` now fetches 50 reviews
(was 3) to compute an accurate `reviews_awaiting_reply` count, still shows only the
top 3 for display. New test: `tests/test_reviews_reply_radar.py`.

**Phase 5 — bundle-opportunity nudge.** The report's narrative example (planners) was
already stale by the time this was built: `BUNDLE_PLANNERS` already covers the 4
active DP10xx listings. Counted directly from `data/product_catalog.json` instead of
trusting the narrative, and found the real gap: `wall_art` has 67 active listings
against a single 3-piece bundle; `coloring_pages` and `paper_pack` have 12-13 active
listings and zero bundles. New deterministic rule (no LLM, just counting) flags a
category when active count ≥10 and the active-to-bundle ratio is ≥15, surfaced on the
mobile Today tab in its own "Opportunities" section — deliberately separate from
"Needs attention" since a growth nudge isn't a problem and shouldn't share
severity-dot styling with an actual alert. New endpoint `GET /api/bundle-
opportunities` (1h cache — catalog structure changes rarely). New test:
`tests/test_bundle_opportunities.py`.

**Phase 6 — one-tap bulk-approve for low-risk pending items.** Scott's confirmed safe
reframing of "confidence-tiered auto-apply" (see course correction above). A narrow
whitelist (`update_tags`/`update_title` only — never price, publish, or anything
CLAUDE.md hard-gates) gets a single "Approve all N" button when 2+ qualify, still
gated by one `confirm()` and deferring to the existing over-limit warning rather than
offering a shortcut past it. No new backend endpoint — batches the exact same
`POST /api/queue/{id}/approve` call N times instead of once, sequentially. New test:
`tests/test_bulk_approve_low_risk.py`.

**Verify:** `python -m py_compile` on all touched `.py` files; inline `<script>`
extracted from the real (business_config-substituted) `_FRANK_HUD_MOCKUP` runtime
string and `node --check`'d clean at every phase boundary, not just once at the end;
full `tests/run_all.py` (46/46, including all 5 new test files); `tools/check_
hardcoded_paths.py` clean; `tools/playwright_smoke.py` green across 2 consecutive
runs; manual Playwright screenshots confirmed the System Health split (desktop
Approvals) and the Opportunities section with the real wall_art/coloring_pages
numbers (mobile Today) render correctly with zero console errors. `_BUILD_ID` bumped
v225→v226.

**Lesson for next time:** when implementing recommendations from a prior research
artifact, re-verify each one's narrative examples against live data before building —
the bundle-opportunity nudge's planner example had already gone stale (a bundle
shipped between the audit and the implementation pass), and building against the real
current catalog surfaced a much stronger, more honest finding (wall_art, not
planners) than the one the report originally wrote up.

## 2026-07-18 — Motion & Flow Audit shipped (research artifact -> implementation, top to bottom)
Scott asked for a follow-up UX pass on Frank's own tap-through feel ("some smoothness that can be put into it... sliding across the highlights tab buttons") after the earlier competitive audit. Researched motion patterns from apps built around interaction polish (sliding tab-bar indicators, directional vs. crossfade transitions, optimistic UI limits, 2026 onboarding research) and published a "Frank — Motion & Flow Audit" artifact with 2 of the findings built live as interactive demos. Scott: "Started at the top and work your way down." Implemented all 5 actionable findings against frank_hud_mockup.py:

1. Sliding pill indicator behind the active bottom tab (`#ptab-pill`, positioned via a MutationObserver watching `.ptab.on` so it stays correct regardless of which of the 3 independent call sites — phoneTab()/openFrankPopup()/phoneOpenScreen() — last changed the active tab).
2. Entrance/exit motion on the product review modal (`prm-in` keyframe both directions; exit needed a JS-coordinated third class, `product-review-closing`, since a `display:none` cut can't be reversed by CSS alone once the open class is removed).
3. In-flight loading state on Approve/bulk-approve (`_setApproveLoading()`) — deliberately NOT optimistic UI (approving a real Etsy write is exactly the irreversible/high-stakes case that pattern excludes); just an honest "Approving…" + disabled button so a slow response doesn't read as a dead tap.
4. A haptic tick (`navigator.vibrate`) on tab switches and a successful approve — Android-only, safe no-op on iOS.
5. A genuinely finished tour (not Skipped) now hands off to one real pending approval if one exists, instead of closing on a static "you're all set" card.

One explicit non-change: kept the existing crossfade on top-level tab switches rather than adding directional slide there — current motion-design research is explicit that crossfade is correct for a dashboard's peer destinations, and slide is for a genuine back-able stack, which Frank's 5 tabs aren't.

**Lesson for next time:** running the local test suite (`tests/run_all.py`) spins up real server subprocesses that exercise the health-check loop, and `_OPS_RUNBOOK_PATH` falls back to writing directly into this committed file when no Railway volume is present locally — a `git status` before staging caught ~50 lines of synthetic `TESTCRASH`/`TESTHUNG`/tmp-path noise that would otherwise have been committed. Worth eventually pointing local test runs at a throwaway path instead of relying on catching it by hand each time.

New test: `tests/test_motion_flow_audit.py` (structural checks against the HUD source, same pattern as the other frontend-only feature tests). Verified: py_compile, node --check on the properly-extracted (Python-string-evaluated, not regex-on-raw-source) inline script, full `tests/run_all.py` (47/47), `tools/check_hardcoded_paths.py`, the standing `tools/playwright_smoke.py`, plus an ad hoc real-browser check confirming the pill's computed transform/opacity actually changes on tab switch and the modal's display sequence is flex → flex (closing) → none.

## 2026-07-18 — SOC 2 / HIPAA / GDPR compliance hardening pass
Scott asked to "make sure" the business is compliant on SOC, HIPAA, and GDPR. Scoped via 3 clarifying questions: HIPAA is precautionary (no health-data feature exists), no external trigger (general due diligence), SOC 2 goal is hardening controls not a certified audit. Research (1 Explore agent + direct verification of its highest-stakes claims myself, not just trusting the summary) found:

- **HIPAA confirmed inapplicable** — no code path anywhere receives/stores a filled-in planner or any customer health data; the Fitness & Wellness Planner is a blank template filled in on the buyer's own device. No engineering work needed.
- **GDPR: found and fixed a real false claim.** privacy.html / tools/api_server/static/privacy.html said "No personal data belonging to customers or third parties is collected or retained" — false, since get_orders returns a real buyer name and order_notifier.py/etsy_autoresponder.py/review_monitor.py touch buyer names and message text. Rewrote both (kept byte-identical, as before) to accurately disclose what's collected, why, retention, and a deletion-request path.
- Verified the existing PII-minimization work (_PII_TOOLS/_should_persist_chat_turn, main.py) is complete, not stale: only get_orders and get_reviews touch buyer-adjacent data at all (grepped every registered agent tool), get_reviews correctly excluded (no buyer identifier in its payload), and get_orders' own handler (not just its tool description) verified to genuinely drop email/address before the model ever sees it.
- Checked the one thing that would have been a real live exposure: data/hub_db_backups/hub_db_state.json is committed to this **public** repo. Pulled all 3 historical versions, scanned every action_queue/activity_log entry (450 combined in the largest) for emails/buyer keywords/order data — zero hits, past or present. No fix needed, but confirmed rather than assumed.
- Added `_prune_buyer_data_retention()` (main.py, runs daily via _quality_audit_iteration): deletes drafted-reply files older than 90 days, caps the two ID-only dedupe files (notified_orders.json, message_drafts/sent_log.json) to their most recent 2,000 entries.
- Added `data/notified_orders.json` to .gitignore (was untracked but unprotected).
- **SOC 2: encrypted etsy_tokens at rest.** Was plaintext in SQLite — the strongest real gap found. Used PyNaCl SecretBox (already a pinned dependency via tools/ci_refresh_etsy_secrets.py, no new package needed) keyed by a new TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY env var; falls back to plaintext (same as before) when unset, and a pre-existing plaintext row decrypts as a transparent pass-through then gets re-saved encrypted on the next hourly OAuth refresh — no manual migration step. Verified all 4 paths (plaintext mode, encrypted mode, legacy-row migration, missing-key-on-encrypted-row hard failure) with a standalone round-trip script before trusting it.
- Wrote a real "Incident Response" section (top of this file) — this codebase has already had a prior real secret leak (per backup_hub_db.py's own comments) and a prior security incident (test_security_headers.py's docstring), so a concrete rotate/scope/notify procedure was a genuine gap, not theoretical.
- Wrote data/knowledge_base/compliance_notes.md: the HIPAA conclusion with reasoning, GDPR posture (implemented + explicitly what's NOT resolved — the controller/processor legal question needs a lawyer if it ever matters), and a SOC 2 Trust-Services-Criteria-style controls inventory naming what a real audit would additionally require (a CPA firm, formal policy docs, etc.) so it's clear what's out of scope, not silently missing.

**Lesson for next time (recurring):** running the local test suite polluted this file with ~65 lines of synthetic test-server health-loop noise again (same class of issue logged 2026-07-18 in the motion-audit entry) — caught via `git status`/`git diff` before staging, file reverted and the intentional edit re-applied cleanly. Worth actually fixing (point local test runs at a throwaway ops-runbook path) rather than catching it by hand a third time.

New test: tests/test_compliance_hardening.py. Verified: py_compile, full tests/run_all.py (48/48), tools/check_hardcoded_paths.py, manual diff-read of the rewritten privacy.html against the actual data flows documented above.


## 2026-07-18 — Self-service signup + account deletion
Scott sent Frank to testers, who hit a dead end: the only account-creation flow (_SETUP_PAGE) is a strict one-time "create the owner account" screen gated on hub_users being empty (main.py's login_page()) — after Scott's own account existed, every new visitor just saw an existing-login-only form with no way in. The admin-panel UI that could create additional accounts was removed 2026-07-11 when this was still a solo shop.

Confirmed (AskUserQuestion): signup is open to anyone with the link (small test group, no gating), and new accounts get the same full access Scott's own account has — same real orders/revenue/buyer-name data, same ability to approve real Etsy writes. Implemented:

- New `/signup` GET+POST routes (main.py) — always available once an owner exists (redirects to /login if hub_users is genuinely empty, so the very first-ever account still goes through the existing one-time owner-setup flow, untouched). Collects email, name, username, password per Scott's spec; creates role="admin" accounts (never "owner" — that stays one-per-shop, created only at first-run setup).
- hub_users gained `email`/`display_name` columns (db.py migration, nullable, old rows unaffected).
- `/login`'s cross-link now always offers "New here? Create an account" once an owner exists (was previously only shown while the table was empty) — this is the actual fix for what Scott's testers hit.
- New self-service `DELETE /api/account` (a buyer-data-adjacent GDPR/CCPA right-to-erasure feature, not an ADA one as Scott initially framed it — corrected this plainly since I'd just written compliance_notes.md and didn't want to bake a wrong compliance claim into it). Identity comes from the session (mirrors change_my_password's pattern exactly), blocks self-deletion of the owner role (would orphan the shop with no one able to manage other users), revokes all sessions on success.
- New Settings "Your Account & Access" card: shows who's signed in (name/username/email/role) and the delete button, disabled with an explanation for the owner account.

**Real test bug caught before shipping:** my first version of `tests/test_signup_and_account_deletion.py` tried to test the owner-block path by logging in via the ENABLE_TEST_LOGIN-seeded account — which is actually role="admin" ("full admin access" per its own startup log), not "owner". The test ran self-delete against it, it correctly succeeded (admin self-delete is supposed to work), which emptied hub_users and cascaded into every other test failing (`/signup` correctly redirects to `/login` when the table is empty). The implementation was never wrong — the test used the wrong seeded role. Fixed by creating a dedicated, separate role="owner" account in test setup instead of repurposing the shared seeded one.

**Lesson for next time (recurring, 3rd occurrence):** running the local test suite polluted this file with ~65 lines of synthetic health-loop noise again during this same work session (also logged in the two prior 2026-07-18 entries above). Caught and reverted each time via `git status`/`git diff` before staging. This is worth actually fixing now rather than continuing to catch it by hand — point local test runs at a throwaway ops-runbook path instead of letting `db.resolve_persistent_path()` fall back to this committed file when no Railway volume is present locally.

Verified: py_compile, node --check on extracted inline JS, full tests/run_all.py (49/49), tools/check_hardcoded_paths.py, tools/playwright_smoke.py, plus a real-browser walkthrough of the full flow (signup → recovery code → Settings shows correct identity → self-delete → redirected to /login).


## 2026-07-18 — Business Tracker workbook (.xlsx) + desktop layout usability

Scott asked what else could improve Frank's setup, specifically desktop usability, and asked for one Excel workbook covering products/COGS/orders in multiple tabs, accessible from the desktop.

**Business Tracker workbook.** Resurrected the archived `tools/generate_business_tracker.py` (trashed 2026-07-11 as an unwired one-off — it hardcoded a stale product snapshot and wrote to gitignored `data/backups/`, so it never reached the hosted deploy) as a new pure builder module, `tools/business_tracker.py`, wired to real data instead:
- **Products** — from `data/product_catalog.json` (live source of truth) instead of a hardcoded 2026-05 snapshot.
- **COGS & Profit** — every active listing via `_estimate_listing_economics()` (the same fee/COGS math already powering the `/api/cogs-status` HUD card), not just the top-5 that endpoint surfaces.
- **Orders** — live, last 100 paid receipts, pulled fresh from Etsy on every download (Scott's explicit choice over an aggregated-only view).
- Physical Inventory / Consumables & Reorder / Suppliers / Equipment & Assets / Expense & Tax Tracker carried over from the archived script mostly unchanged — no live data source exists for these, so they stay honest blank templates rather than fake "live" tabs.

New `GET /api/business-tracker.xlsx` endpoint generates the workbook in memory (`io.BytesIO`, never written to disk) on every request and streams it back with a `Content-Disposition: attachment` header; best-effort on the live-data fetches (an Etsy outage degrades those sheets to empty rather than failing the whole download, same tolerance `_sales_by_listing_sync()` already applies). New "Reports & Export" card in Settings with a download button, reachable from both desktop and mobile. Added `openpyxl==3.1.5` as a real pinned dependency (was previously deliberately excluded since the old script was a one-off).

While building this, found and closed a real duplication: `_sales_by_listing_sync()` and `_search_orders()` were each independently fetching+caching the identical last-100-receipts Etsy call under two different cache keys. Consolidated into one shared `_get_recent_orders_raw()` (cache key `orders_recent`, 120s TTL) that all three callers (including the new Orders tab) now use.

**Desktop usability.** Investigated two hypotheses from static code reading, live-verified before touching anything:
- *"Dashboard gated behind a hamburger click"* — turned out to be **already fixed** (a 2026-07-15 change auto-opens it on first desktop load). Live Playwright check confirmed `cc-open` is present before first paint, sidebar genuinely visible, zero flash, across a fresh authenticated session. No code change made — would have been wasted/redundant work.
- *"Fixed 1440×900 stage only ever gets visually scaled, wasting space on wide monitors"* — this one was real. `#stage`'s layout size is now dynamic (clamped between the original 1440×900 floor and an 1800×1000 ceiling, tracking the viewport in between) instead of a hardcoded constant that only ever got `transform: scale()`d bigger. `.screen`/`.panel` already had no hardcoded pixel widths (sized by the grid's `226px 1fr` track), so they picked up the extra real width for free. Verified at 1440×900 (unchanged), 1920×1080 (stage grows to 1800×1000, ~30% more real content width), 3440×1440 ultrawide (capped at the ceiling, correctly centered with symmetric margins — measured via `getBoundingClientRect`, not just eyeballed off a downscaled screenshot, which read misleadingly asymmetric), and 1024×768 (still scales down exactly as before, nothing clips). The one previously-flagged risk area, the header alert dropdown ("sized for a 1440px stage" per an old comment), turned out to already be safe — it's positioned `right:0` relative to its own header, not the stage's absolute width — confirmed correctly positioned within the viewport at all four sizes.

**Real regression caught by `tools/playwright_smoke.py` before shipping:** the new `fitStage()` set an inline `stage.style.width`/`height` on desktop but never cleared it on the mobile branch. `tools/playwright_smoke.py` opens a desktop viewport first, then resizes to a mobile one mid-test (the back-to-top button check) — the leftover inline width (e.g. `1440px`) beat the mobile media query's `width:100vw` (only `transform` has `!important` there), breaking the mobile stage's real width and, downstream, `document.body`'s scroll math the back-to-top button depends on. Fixed by clearing `stage.style.width`/`height` in the mobile early-return branch. Full smoke suite green after the fix; this is exactly the kind of thing a real desktop→mobile resize test catches that a fresh-mobile-load test wouldn't.

New test: `tests/test_business_tracker.py` (workbook structure/data-fidelity, the orders-fetch dedup, endpoint auth + content-type + graceful degradation). Verified: py_compile, full `tests/run_all.py` (50/50), `tools/check_hardcoded_paths.py`, `tools/playwright_smoke.py`, plus real-browser end-to-end checks (clicked the actual Settings download button and confirmed a real, valid 9-sheet .xlsx came back cookie-authenticated; measured stage sizing/centering at 4 viewports).

## 2026-07-18 — Google Calendar integration + weekly/monthly ops summary emails

Scott asked to integrate Google Calendar into Frank's Calendar tab so anything on it surfaces as reminders, and what else might be worth adding. Scoped: Google Calendar should be **read + write** (not just pulling events in — Frank also pushes its own deadlines onto the calendar), plus **email the weekly/monthly ops summaries** that already ran automatically but never left the app (real-time SMS/push was considered and declined this round).

**Google Calendar — read + write.** No Google OAuth existed anywhere in this codebase before (only the Gemini API-key SDK, a bearer-token library, not OAuth2). Built:
- `tools/google_calendar_oauth.py` — mirrors `tools/tiktok_oauth.py`'s pattern (a real local `HTTPServer` catching the redirect automatically, `localhost:3006/callback` — a fresh port; 3003/3004/3005 are already Etsy/Pinterest/TikTok). Requires `access_type=offline&prompt=consent` on the auth URL — Google only issues a refresh token on first consent otherwise, a gotcha none of the other 3 OAuth flows in this repo have since none of them are Google.
- `tools/google_calendar_api.py` — a lightweight client (`list_upcoming_events()`, `create_event()`), auto-refreshing, raising a distinct `GoogleCalendarNotConnectedError` so callers can degrade cleanly (not connected vs. a real API failure).
- `db.py` — new `google_calendar_tokens` table (identical shape to `etsy_tokens`, reuses the existing `_encrypt_token`/`_decrypt_token` helpers directly — no new crypto code) and a `google_calendar_synced_events` table (local item key → Google event id) for the write-back dedup below.
- **Read path:** `/api/cadence` gained a `google_calendar` list (new "📅 Google Calendar" section in the Calendar tab, same `_calCard` pattern as the other 3 sections); `/api/alerts` gained near-term (today/tomorrow) events as `source: "google_calendar"` reminders in the bell dropdown — the literal "reminders" behavior asked for, not just a Calendar-tab addition. Both degrade to empty/no-alert, never an error, when not connected or on any real API failure.
- **Write path:** a new `create_calendar_event` agent tool (Scott can ask Frank conversationally to add something), plus a daily step in `_calendar_tasks_loop` (`_sync_calendar_to_google()`) that pushes due-dated to-dos and imminent seasonal/tax deadlines onto the calendar — reuses the exact same data `/api/cadence` already computes, no new data source. The `google_calendar_synced_events` table stops repeated daily runs from creating duplicate events.
- Added to the Connections screen's Platform Roadmap (same pattern as Pinterest/TikTok's "wiring done, only OAuth remains" cards) with its setup steps.
- Real Google OAuth credentials can't be obtained in this sandbox, so the actual "connect and pull my calendar" step is Scott-gated, same as Pinterest/TikTok today — everything up to that point (code, graceful not-connected behavior, all degrade paths) is fully built and tested against mocked API responses.

**Weekly/monthly ops summary emails.** `_run_weekly_monitors()` (Sundays) and `_run_monthly_shop_health()` (1st of month) already ran automatically but only ever wrote an in-app todo + `ops_runbook.md` entry — Scott had to open Frank to see the results. Added `_email_ops_summary()`, which reuses `daily_brief.py`'s existing `_send_brief()` SMTP sender (lazy-imported, same pattern `main.py`'s daily-brief loop already uses) rather than a third independent SMTP implementation (`order_notifier.py` already has its own). Wrapped in try/except so a send failure never blocks the existing todo/ops_runbook write, which must always happen regardless.

New test: `tests/test_google_calendar.py` (token/synced-event storage round-trips, the API client's not-connected/refresh/create-event behavior, `/api/cadence` and `/api/alerts` degrade cleanly and surface near-term events as reminders, the `create_calendar_event` tool works and errors cleanly, the daily auto-sync dedups across runs, the ops-summary email helper calls `_send_brief` and tolerates a send failure). Verified: py_compile, full `tests/run_all.py` (51/51), `tools/check_hardcoded_paths.py`, `tools/playwright_smoke.py` (one transient WebGL-asset-fetch flake on the first run, unrelated to this change, green on retry), plus a real-browser end-to-end check confirming the Calendar tab's new section and its not-connected empty state, and the Connections screen's new Google Calendar roadmap card with its setup steps.

## 2026-07-18 — Bug hunt: 10 real bugs found and fixed across Frank

Scott asked to find bugs in Frank ("there are some but you have to find them"). Ran 3 parallel agent audits — one on the Google Calendar/Business Tracker code just shipped, one on `main.py`'s background loops and status endpoints, one on `frank_hud_mockup.py`'s frontend logic — then personally verified every candidate finding by reading the actual code before trusting it, and reproduced the most severe ones directly (not just trusting agent write-ups). All 10 confirmed bugs got fixed, each with a live reproduction both before and after the fix.

**Google Calendar bugs (all in code shipped hours earlier — freshest, least battle-tested):**
1. `tools/google_calendar_oauth.py` never loaded `.env` — `CLIENT_ID`/`CLIENT_SECRET` were read via bare `os.getenv()` with nothing populating the process environment first, so the script printed "must be set in .env" and refused to start on every single run, even with correct values genuinely present in `.env`. Reproduced live (added real-looking values to `.env`, ran in a clean shell, confirmed the failure; confirmed the fix resolves it the same way). **This alone meant Google Calendar could never actually be connected.**
2. `create_event()`'s all-day branch set `end.date == start.date` — Google's API requires an all-day event's end date to be exclusive (the day after start), so every all-day create (which is every item the daily sync pushes — due-dated todos, seasonal/tax deadlines are all plain dates) would be rejected with a 400. Also gave timed events a real 1-hour duration instead of zero.
3. No boot-time reconciliation of Google Calendar tokens from the DB — unlike Etsy, nothing ever called `db.get_google_calendar_tokens()` at startup, so a Railway restart could silently lose the connection even with a perfectly good refresh token sitting in the durable DB. Added `_reconcile_google_calendar_tokens()`, a simpler sibling of `_reconcile_etsy_tokens()` (no lineage tracking needed — Google's refresh token doesn't invalidate on use).
4. `_sync_calendar_to_google()`'s to-do loop was missing the "already past" guard the seasonal/tax loops right next to it both have — first connect would've backfilled every already-overdue open todo onto the calendar dated in the past.
5. Completing or deleting a synced todo never removed its calendar event — permanently orphaned events. Added `GoogleCalendarClient.delete_event()` and wired cleanup into both `POST /api/todos/{id}/toggle` (on completion) and `DELETE /api/todos/{id}`.

**Pre-existing bugs elsewhere:**
6. `_calendar_tasks_loop`'s "did this already run today" state was in-memory only — a same-day redeploy (this app deploys often) could re-fire that day's weekly/monthly/seasonal task, including a duplicate email and duplicate live Etsy calls. Persisted via `db.settings` (same table `_check_star_seller_status`/`_check_ads_thresholds` already use for their own cooldowns), rehydrated at loop start.
7. `_reconcile_etsy_tokens()`'s lineage check only tracked one generation of `parent_refresh_token` — 2+ reactive rotations without a restart lost track of anything more than one hop back, so a stale Railway env var from 2+ rotations ago could be misidentified as a genuine fresh manual re-auth and left in place (dead token, 401 invalid_grant on next use — the exact 2026-06-17 landmine this mechanism exists to prevent). `db.save_etsy_tokens()` now accumulates a full JSON-encoded lineage list (capped at 20) instead of overwriting a single parent; `parse_token_lineage()` handles both the new format and old plain-string rows. Reproduced the exact A→B→C-without-restart scenario live and confirmed the fix restores the correct current token instead of the dead original.
8. `syncMobileClass()` unconditionally stripped `cc-open` whenever mobile — but `phoneOpenScreen()` (opening a screen from the mobile "More" menu or Create tab) deliberately sets `cc-open` while staying mobile, since that's what makes `.screen` visible at all. Any resize event (iOS Safari's address-bar collapse on scroll is a real, common trigger) while viewing a More-opened screen silently hid the whole screen. First fix attempt gated on `phone-panel` being present, but `tools/playwright_smoke.py`'s own pre-existing regression test caught that this wasn't precise enough (it forces a stray `cc-open` without going through `phoneOpenScreen()`, so `phone-panel` was absent there too despite it not being the legitimate case) — replaced with a dedicated `phone-screen-open` marker set only by `phoneOpenScreen()` and cleared by `phoneTab()`/`closeControlCenter()`, an unambiguous signal. Also fixed that same smoke test's setup: an earlier unrelated section (the back-to-top regression test) left the page in a genuine `phoneOpenScreen()` state with nothing to reset it, which was masking the real bug until the fix's test coverage exposed it — added an explicit `phoneTab('more')` reset before the stuck-`cc-open` check so it actually tests what its own comment claims.
9. Several "is this overdue" checks compared a local `due_date` string against `new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)`, which is always the UTC date, not the browser's local date. For any US timezone (this shop's operating region), evening hours are already the next UTC day — a task due "today" got flagged overdue starting ~5-8pm local, hours early. Added a `_localDateStr()` helper and replaced all 3 call sites; reproduced with a `timezone_id: "America/New_York"` browser context and a 9pm-Eastern timestamp that's already the next UTC day, confirming the old code would have gotten it wrong and the new code doesn't.
10. `bulkApproveLowRisk()` only disabled its own "Approve all" button, leaving each candidate's individual Approve/Reject buttons live for the whole multi-second bulk run — a double-tap fired a second `approveAction()` for something the bulk loop had already (or was about to) approve. The backend's `status != "pending"` guard on `/api/queue/{id}/approve` already prevents a real duplicate apply, so this was a confusing error-toast bug, not a data-integrity one — still fixed by giving each candidate's button a stable id and disabling the row via the same `_setApproveLoading()` helper individual cards already use.

Verified: py_compile on every touched file, full `tests/run_all.py` (51/51 — 2 tests updated for necessary behavior changes: `parent_refresh_token`'s new JSON-lineage format, plus one new regression test for the 2-generations-back scenario), `tools/check_hardcoded_paths.py`, `tools/playwright_smoke.py` (green twice in a row after the test-setup fix), plus live reproduction scripts for items 1, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 specifically (not just unit tests — actual before/after behavioral proof for the ones with a real-world trigger to reproduce).


## 2026-07-18 — Wordmark: solid transparent fill instead of wireframe

Scott sent a screenshot of the mobile orb screen — the "OnBrandCraftz" 3D wordmark was rendering as a wireframe/line mesh (every triangle edge of the extruded letterforms traced as a visible line) and asked for a solid-but-transparent look instead, no line design.

Root cause: `initOrbGL()`'s `THREE.ShaderMaterial` for the wordmark mesh had `wireframe: true` (main.py history: this was inherited from the original noise-displaced icosahedron "orb" concept, where a wireframe look made sense for a sphere — never revisited when the mesh became solid extruded letterforms on 2026-07-18 earlier the same day). Fixed: `wireframe: false`, plus added `side: THREE.DoubleSide` so the letters stay filled-looking through the wordmark's full rotation (the extrusion's back faces would otherwise cull to nothing under the default `FrontSide` on the far half of each spin). `transparent: true` and the existing `uOpacity: 0.85` uniform were already in place, so no other change was needed to get the "solid but transparent" look. `_rebuildWordmarkForPairing()` (fired when Scott changes font pairing in Settings) reuses this same material object rather than creating its own, so the fix covers every font pairing automatically.

Verified: py_compile, full `tests/run_all.py` (51/51), `tools/check_hardcoded_paths.py`, `tools/playwright_smoke.py`, plus a real-browser screenshot confirming the letters render as a solid filled glow with no wireframe lines.


## 2026-07-18 — Products screen: file-integrity root cause, dead-end taps fixed, gray header overlay, multi-category "Build whole product"

Scott sent 3 screenshots: (1) Products cards need a real action when tapped, not a dead end; (2) only 5/176 catalog products showed "all files present" — "figure that out"; (3) a gray block was rendering over the header on Products and Create; (4) "Build whole product" only worked for planners, wanted it for other listing types too.

**Root cause of the 5/176 stat — a path bug, not missing content.** `_product_file_exists()`/`_build_products_status()` only understood catalog paths starting with `data/digital_products/`. An audit of the real catalog found almost every non-planner category's file paths live outside that prefix: `wall_art` 101/104 refs, `coloring_pages` 19/19, `paper_pack` 12/12, `uncategorized` 13/13, `svg_3dprint_pack` 2/2, `svg_bundle` 4/4 — most were either mis-joined into a nonsense double-nested path (paths with a directory, e.g. `data/svg_pack/...`) or, more commonly, bare filenames with **no directory at all** (`coloring_set_01.zip`, `DP1063_print_sizes.zip`) whose real location varies unpredictably per product (e.g. `SS1001_america250_3dprint_pack_vol1.zip` actually lives under `data/3d_print_signs/america_250/`, unrelated to its own filename). `tools/sync_files_to_hub.py` (the script that pushes local files to the Railway volume) had the identical narrowness — `SRC_DIR` only ever walked `data/digital_products/`, so files for every other category could never reach the volume regardless of whether they existed on Scott's machine.

**Fix:** new `_catalog_file_exists()`/`_catalog_file_abs_path()`/`_catalog_file_url()` in `main.py` handle all three conventions found in the real catalog — legacy prefixed (delegates to the original `_product_file_exists()`, unchanged), explicit non-prefixed paths (checked against the repo root + volume), and bare filenames (resolved via a new cached, 5-min-TTL basename index built by `rglob`-ing `data/` and the volume, excluding ops/internal dirs like `trash`/`backups`/`financial`). `_build_products_status()` now hands the raw catalog path straight to the checker instead of pre-stripping a single prefix. `tools/sync_files_to_hub.py` now walks all of `data/` (same exclude list) instead of just `data/digital_products/`, preserving the legacy relative-path convention for files that were already there and using the full repo-root-relative path for everything else. `3d_print_physical` and the two `*_license` categories were never supposed to have a "files" array (physical goods ship, license listings grant a license not a design file) — excluded from the gate via `_NO_FILES_REQUIRED_CATEGORIES`, with an honest badge instead of the old confusing "no files listed" one.

**Etsy-first verification for what's still missing:** new `tools/audit_product_files.py` — for every `active` catalog entry still missing files after the path fix, calls `EtsyAPIClient.get_listing_files()` (read-only) and classifies into `verified_live` (Etsy has real files, just a missing local backup — not urgent) vs `genuinely_missing` (neither Etsy nor local disk has anything — the real "customer might be getting nothing" compliance case). Writes a report to the persistent volume; `GET /api/alerts` reads it and surfaces `genuinely_missing` entries as `source: "product_file_integrity"` critical alerts — a visible punch list, not a buried percentage. Per CLAUDE.md's top-priority rule, nothing auto-regenerates content for a listing verified live on Etsy or genuinely missing — that's Scott's call.

**Every product-card tap now leads to a real action.** `openProductFixSheet()` extended beyond digital_planner-only: `wall_art`/`wall_art_bundle` and `coloring_pages` now get real "🤖 Regenerate" buttons (reusing `/api/produce/print-zip` and a new `/api/produce/coloring-pack` background endpoint). Categories with no verified generator this round show the honest `file_audit` state (✅ verified live on Etsy, ⚠️ flagged for review, or ℹ️ not yet checked) instead of a fake button — never a silent dead end.

**Gray header overlay — traced live via Playwright, not the initially-suspected `#alert-dropdown`.** The orb is the mobile home tab at load (`setTimeout(() => phoneTab('ask'), 0)` sets `frank-popup-open` on every mobile page load), but `phoneOpenScreen()` (every "More" list item, including Products) never cleared it — body ended up with both `frank-popup-open` and `cc-open` at once, and `body.is-mobile.frank-popup-open #orb-view`'s CSS (2 classes) outranked `body.cc-open #orb-view{display:none}` (1 class) by specificity, so the full-screen orb popup (translucent radial-gradient background) rendered on top of the header — confirmed live when a Playwright click on the bell icon timed out because the orb's stage was intercepting pointer events. Fixed by clearing `frank-popup-open`/`overflow` inside `phoneOpenScreen()` itself. Extended `tools/playwright_smoke.py` to assert both `#alert-dropdown`'s vertical position (it was never actually the culprit, but had no vertical-overlap coverage either) and that `frank-popup-open`/`#orb-view` are cleared after `phoneOpenScreen()`.

**"Build whole product" generalized beyond planners.** `_produce_build_product()` now resolves a category (explicit or looked up from the catalog by pid) and dispatches: `digital_planner` unchanged (`build_product.py`); new `tools/build_wallart_product.py` (print-size ZIP → QC) and `tools/build_coloring_product.py` (theme pages + ZIP sets → QC, pack derived from the product's own filename convention). Both deliberately skip the 10-listing-photos step this round (a separate, already category-agnostic tool exists for that) and say so in their own output rather than silently doing less than the copy implies. Every other category returns a clear error instead of guessing. Create-screen copy updated to list exactly what's wired per category.

Verified: py_compile, full `tests/run_all.py` (52/52 — 2 pre-existing tests updated for the new `file_exists_fn` contract, 1 new test file `test_products_file_integrity.py`), `tools/playwright_smoke.py` (green, including the new gray-overlay regression coverage), live-browser screenshots confirming the header renders clean and the Create screen's updated copy.

**CI-only follow-up (same day):** CI Smoke failed after the push above — a fresh checkout has no `.env` file (never git-committed, by design), and `tools/generate_planner.py` unconditionally did `with open(_ENV_PATH) as _f:` with no existence guard, unlike every other tool script's dotenv loader in this codebase. Anything importing `generate_planner_v2` (the digital-planner build path, exercised directly for the first time by the new `test_digital_planner_path_unchanged` test) crashed with `FileNotFoundError` wherever `.env` doesn't exist on disk — which is also genuinely how Railway itself works (env vars injected by the platform, no `.env` file shipped), so this was a real latent production risk for the planner-build feature, not just a CI artifact. Fixed with the same `if os.path.exists(...):` guard the rest of the codebase already uses. Also fixed 2 of the new tests that assumed `data/digital_products/product_files/DP1030*` exist on disk — real product PDFs/ZIPs are never git-committed (only `data/svg_pack/`, `data/3d_print_signs/`, etc. are), so a fresh CI checkout has none of them; both now write a self-contained temp fixture instead. Verified by removing `.env` locally and re-running the full suite (all green) before re-pushing.


## 2026-07-19 — Etsy Listing Files: real inventory of what's attached to live listings, not local storage

Scott corrected a misunderstanding from the previous round: he wanted the Files tab to show every file from the actual Etsy listings, not Frank's own local/generated file storage (the "SAVED FILES (PERSISTENT)" section he screenshotted is a browser over `data/digital_products/` + the volume, not Etsy).

**Hard platform limit, confirmed before building anything:** Etsy's Open API v3 has no endpoint to download a listing's digital file content — `GET .../listings/{id}/files` returns metadata only (filename, size, rank, upload date), never bytes, and there's no separate download-content endpoint. This isn't new — this repo's own `ops_runbook.md` already documented hitting this exact wall twice (2026-06-19, 2026-06-20) trying to restore lost local backups. Confirmed with Scott before implementing: the feature would show real file names/sizes from Etsy, and offer a genuine download only where a same-named file happens to already exist locally — clearly labeled as a local copy, never claimed to be a live pull from Etsy.

**Built:**
- `tools/etsy_file_inventory.py` — sweeps every `status: active` catalog product with a real `etsy_listing_id`, calls the already-existing `EtsyAPIClient.get_listing_files()` (read-only), and writes a report (`etsy_file_inventory_report.json`, same durable-volume/`data/` fallback convention as `tools/audit_product_files.py`). Unlike that script, this is a full inventory, not a gap-audit — it records every active listing's files regardless of local status, including a genuinely-zero-files listing (kept distinct from "skipped" — no listing id or an API error — so an API hiccup can never be misread as "this listing has no files").
- `main.py`: `_etsy_file_inventory_report()` reader (same missing/corrupt-file tolerance as the existing `_file_audit_report()`), `_build_etsy_files_response()` cross-references each Etsy-reported filename against `_catalog_filename_index()` (the bare-filename lookup built for the Products-screen fix two rounds ago) to set `local_match`/`local_url` per file, and `GET /api/etsy-files` serves the result.
- `_run_etsy_file_inventory_sweep()` wired into `_calendar_tasks_loop()`'s daily block (same `_get_calendar_task_last_run`/`_set_calendar_task_last_run` persisted-cooldown pattern as `star_seller_check`/`ads_check`) so the report refreshes automatically once a day.
- Frontend: a new "Etsy Listing Files (live from Etsy)" section on the Files screen, collapsible per-listing groups (reuses the existing `toggleZip()` pattern, own `_etsyFilesGrpSeq` counter to avoid an id-collision race with `loadFiles()`'s concurrent `_hubGrpSeq` reset — both loaders now run together via `_SCREEN_LOADERS.files`). Each file row shows name + size and either a real "⬇ Local copy" download link or an honest "🔗 View on Etsy" link when no local match exists — verified end-to-end via a live Playwright run with a seeded report + a matching local fixture file, confirming the DOM renders exactly the local-match vs. no-match state correctly.

Verified: py_compile, full `tests/run_all.py` (53/53, including a new `test_etsy_file_inventory.py` — sweep classification against a mocked Etsy client, report-reader tolerance, local-match cross-referencing, daily-sweep write, and loop/endpoint wiring checks), re-ran the whole suite with `.env` removed again (the CI failure mode from the previous entry) to confirm no repeat, `tools/playwright_smoke.py`, and a live-browser DOM inspection of the populated Etsy Listing Files section showing correct local-copy vs. view-on-Etsy states.


## 2026-07-21 — Reliability sweep: background-loop and chat-agent resilience audit

Scott's instruction: "Research better pathways and also loops that make all agents better. Make sure everything is solid." Ran 3 parallel research agents over the 7 background loops (`_snapshot_loop`, `_warm_suggestions`, `_token_sync_loop`, `_quality_audit_loop`, `_health_check_loop`, `_daily_brief_loop`, `_calendar_tasks_loop`), the chat agent's tool-calling loop (`_run_agent_turn`), and the resilience infrastructure backing external API calls (`resilience.py`, `etsy_api.py`, `image_gen.py`). Fixed every well-scoped, high-confidence bug found — 14 fixes total, each with its own new/extended test:

1. **`_execute_agent_tool`'s `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` handler had a NameError** — referenced an undefined `timeout` name instead of the caught exception's own `.timeout` attribute; a timed-out exec command crashed instead of reporting cleanly.
2. **504 missing from retryable Etsy statuses** — `resilience.py`'s `_RETRYABLE_ETSY_STATUSES` had `{403, 429, 500, 502, 503}`; a 504 gateway timeout (which `get_conversion_targets`/`diagnose_listing_conversion`/`apply_conversion_fixes` can hit) was misclassified as non-retryable.
3. **Chat round-trip cap exhaustion corrupted `history`** — the 6-round tool-call cap had nothing after it; if round 6 was itself `tool_use`, the loop ended with `history` on a user-role message, so the next real user turn appended a second consecutive user-role message and Anthropic 400'd ("roles must alternate"), permanently wedging that session. Fixed with one guaranteed final round offering no `tools` param, so `stop_reason` can never be `tool_use` on the last round.
4. **PII gap for `execute_command`-wrapped order tools** — `check_new_orders`/`send_order_notifications`/`check_buyer_messages` return real buyer PII in stdout, but the wrapper tool name is always `execute_command`, so the PII-tracking check (which only looked at `block.name`) never caught them. Added `contains_pii` to their `_EXEC_COMMANDS` entries and a check against the underlying command name.
5. **`_daily_brief_loop`'s in-memory `last_sent_date`** — reset to `None` on every restart (duplicate same-day send risk) and the manual `/api/brief/run` endpoint never synced it. Persisted via the existing `_get_calendar_task_last_run`/`_set_calendar_task_last_run` helpers; both the loop and the manual endpoint now read/write the same gate.
6. **`_calendar_tasks_loop`'s aggregate heartbeat lied on sub-task failure** — always reported `"ok"` regardless of whether any of its sub-tasks actually failed. Now tracks `failed` explicitly; a real failure can never render as a false "ok".
7. **Stale "5-minute health loop" strings** — 5 user/ops-facing strings still said "5-minute" after the loop was changed to hourly; fixed (4 unrelated "5 minute" mentions elsewhere referring to a different historical incident were correctly left alone).
8. **`_warm_suggestions` race with `_suggestions_warming`** — the manual `POST /api/suggestions` path already checked the in-flight guard before spawning a compute, but the *scheduled* tick never did, so a scheduled fire coinciding with a manual request could run two ~25s Anthropic syntheses concurrently. Added the same guard to the scheduled path.
9. **`listing_manifest.json` non-atomic write + stale-snapshot race** — plain `open(...,"w")` (torn-write risk on crash) plus a snapshot read at the start of a run that could clobber a concurrent run's updates. Extracted `_write_manifest_updates()`: re-reads fresh right before merging, writes via `.tmp` + `.replace()`.
10. **Ideogram calls had zero retry/error handling** — two bare `urllib.request.urlopen()` calls (generate + image download) with no try/except at all, unlike every other engine in `image_gen.py`. Added `_get_bytes()` (mirrors `_post()`'s retry/backoff) and routed both calls through the existing retry policy.
11. **No timeout ceiling around chat tool dispatch** — `asyncio.to_thread(_execute_agent_tool, ...)` had no bound; most `_EXEC_COMMANDS` branches are subprocess-timeout-bounded (max 400s), but others (e.g. `video_understanding.py`'s yt-dlp download and Gemini file-upload poll loop) have zero timeout of their own and could wedge a whole chat turn forever. Wrapped in `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=480s)`; a trip degrades to a normal error `tool_result` instead of hanging (the underlying thread can't be force-killed, same tradeoff `_dispatch_to_relay` already makes).
12. **Silent prune/sub-task failures in `_snapshot_loop` and `_quality_audit_loop`** — the daily trash-vault + rate-limit-log prune, and the quality-audit loop's buyer-data retention prune / KB rotation / recurring-failures promotion / DB record, all failed print()-only with no heartbeat — invisible outside server logs. A silently-broken buyer-data retention pass in particular is a real compliance concern (retention rule), not just maintenance trivia. Both loops now fold any sub-task failure into their existing heartbeat as a `"warning"` (never overriding a real `"error"`, and never affecting the primary job's own success/backoff timing — a deliberate existing design choice preserved as-is).
13. **Etsy image/video/file uploads had zero retry** — `upload_listing_image`/`upload_listing_video`/`upload_listing_file` each built a raw multipart body and called `urlopen()` exactly once, unlike every JSON API call in the client (`_request_impl`: 3-attempt backoff, 429/503 retry, capped Retry-After). These uploads put the actual product photos/video/digital file live on a listing — arguably the highest-value calls in the client — so a transient blip or an ordinary 429/503 failed the whole upload outright. Extracted `_upload_multipart_with_retry()` mirroring `_request_impl`'s policy; all three now route through it.
14. **`_run_loop_iteration`'s error-path heartbeat write could cascade-kill a loop** — the `except` branch's own `db.set_agent_heartbeat(..., "error", ...)` call was unguarded; if that write itself raised (DB disk full, locked file — exactly the kind of condition likely to coincide with a real incident), the exception propagated out of `_run_loop_iteration` uncaught (every one of the 5 real background loops calls it with nothing wrapping the call), permanently killing that loop's asyncio task until a full process restart. Wrapped in its own try/except that logs and swallows.

Deliberately deferred (out of scope this round, no code changed): none — all 14 identified fixes were completed.

Verified: py_compile on every changed file, full `tests/run_all.py` (61/61, including 9 new test files: `test_chat_turn_roundtrip_cap.py`, extensions to `test_chat_pii_persistence.py` and `test_listing_integrity.py`, `test_calendar_tasks_heartbeat_honesty.py`, `test_warm_suggestions_race.py`, `test_image_gen_ideogram_retry.py`, `test_chat_tool_dispatch_timeout.py`, `test_loop_subtask_heartbeat_visibility.py`, `test_etsy_upload_retry.py`, `test_run_loop_iteration_heartbeat_resilience.py`, plus 2 pre-existing tests updated for the new `_quality_audit_skip_result`/subtask-failures shape), `tools/playwright_smoke.py` (green).

Defaults to a dry run; `--execute` without `--yes` prompts for confirmation first. Writes a timestamped report to `data/reports/`. ## 2026-07-21 — File Integrity Audit loop: closing a dead feature (audit built, never scheduled)

Scott asked what else could be made better in Frank -- "better loops with better checks that run with higher quality." Found a real, concrete gap while investigating: `tools/audit_product_files.py`'s live-Etsy file-integrity audit (the function that classifies each active digital listing's file status as `verified_live`/`genuinely_missing`), the `product_file_integrity` critical alert source in `/api/alerts`, and the Products-screen per-card `file_audit` badge had all shipped in earlier rounds — but **nothing ever actually called `audit()` in production**. It only ran if someone manually typed `python tools/audit_product_files.py` from a machine with real Etsy credentials, which never happened live. Confirmed: `data/file_audit_report.json` never existed, so `_file_audit_report()` always returned `None`, so the alert and every Products-screen badge were silently dead from the day they shipped.

**Fix:** new `_file_audit_loop()` background loop (8th real loop, registered alongside the other 7 at startup) runs the audit once a day via the shared `_run_loop_iteration()` retry/backoff/heartbeat helper every other loop already uses, and writes the report atomically. New `POST /api/file-audit/run` lets Scott force an immediate refresh from the dashboard (matching the existing `/api/calendar-tasks/run`/`/api/brief/run` manual-trigger pattern) right after fixing a flagged listing, instead of waiting up to 24h for the badge to clear. Heartbeat reports `"error"` when a listing is genuinely missing (the real compliance risk), `"warning"` when the audit hit skips (API/auth errors, so coverage is incomplete) but nothing is confirmed missing, `"ok"` on a fully clean run.

Implementation note: `_file_audit_iteration()` imports `audit_product_files` lazily (inside the function, not at main.py's top level) — that module does `import main as _main` to reuse this file's own `_build_products_status()`/`_catalog_file_exists()`/`_product_catalog_overrides()` helpers rather than duplicating them, which would be a circular import at module load time. By the time the loop actually runs (well after startup), `main` is already fully initialized in `sys.modules`, so the nested import just reuses the live module.

Verified: py_compile, new `tests/test_file_audit_loop.py` (6 tests — atomic report write, error/warning/ok heartbeat classification, manual-endpoint auth gate + response shape), full `tests/run_all.py` (63/63), `tools/playwright_smoke.py`.
