## 2026-07-25 — Coloring pages: stage real pack pages as Etsy listing photos (COLOR1003 had none)

**Symptom (Scott, live):** COLOR1003 published successfully as an Etsy draft but had zero listing photos. Not a bug — a known, already-disclosed gap (the review modal's own info banner already said "Listing photos aren't auto-generated for Coloring Pages yet"), since the only existing AI listing-photo pipeline (`_produce_listing_photos()` / `gen_planner_listing_photos.py`) is hardcoded to digital planners only.

**Scott's direction:** "You upload the images from that pack to the Etsy" — use the real individual coloring-page PNGs already inside the product's own delivered ZIP as the listing photos, not an AI-generated lifestyle mockup. Honest by construction (literally the files the customer receives).

**Real wrinkle found while building this:** the existing photo-staging quality gate (`_check_no_pale_background()`, in `_validate_staged_action`'s `listing_photo` branch) hard-rejects any photo whose 4 corners average >217/255 luminance ("too pale/washed out") — meant to catch lazy/blank AI renders. A raw coloring page is white printer paper by design, so its corners are near-pure-white and would systematically fail this gate. Asked Scott directly (`AskUserQuestion`): raw pages + relax the gate for this category, vs. a composited flat-lay mockup (passes the gate unmodified, more build effort, needs the AI image engine). **Scott chose: raw pages, relax the gate.**

**What shipped:**
- `_check_no_pale_background(path, category="")` — skips the check entirely when `category == "coloring_pages"`, with a dated comment explaining why a pale background is the honest, correct look for this product type. The bypass is category-scoped, not global — confirmed with a regression test that a near-white photo still fails the gate by default and for every other category.
- `category` threaded through `_stage_photo_action()` → the `listing_photo` staged-action payload → `_validate_staged_action`'s pale-background call, so only photos explicitly staged as `coloring_pages` skip the check.
- New `_extract_coloring_page_images(zip_path, n)` — reuses `qc_sweep.coloring_zip_page_count()`'s exact "root-level PNG" file definition (never re-derived by hand); samples up to 10 pages evenly across the pack (not just the first 10) when there are more than Etsy's 10-photo cap.
- New `_produce_coloring_pages_listing_photos(pid)` — resolves the real Etsy `listing_id` via `_gather_product_review()` (reused, not re-derived), finds the product's ZIP via `_catalog_file_abs_path()` (the same three-convention resolver from the file-resolution fix above), extracts real pages, and stages each via `_stage_photo_action(..., category="coloring_pages")` for Scott's one-tap approval — nothing uploads to Etsy without his approval, same as every other mutation.
- `_produce_listing_photos()` now dispatches to the new coloring_pages path at the top (before the planner-specific lookup) — so the *existing* `generate_listing_photos` chat tool and `POST /api/produce/listing-photos` endpoint automatically do the right thing for coloring_pages, zero new tool/endpoint wiring.
- Frontend: the Products review modal's coloring_pages branch now offers a real **"📸 Stage listing photos from pack"** button (only once a `listing_id` exists — nothing to stage against otherwise), wired to `productReviewGenerateColoringPhotos()`. `wall_art`'s photo gap is untouched (separate, still-unsupported issue, out of scope here).

**Verification:** `tests/test_coloring_listing_photos.py` (new, 13 tests) — page extraction/sampling, the category-scoped gate bypass (and that it stays scoped), the core staging function's success/error paths, the `_produce_listing_photos()` dispatch, and the end-to-end `_validate_staged_action` bypass. Full suite 79/79 passed, 3x clean Playwright (new block confirms the button renders only for coloring_pages + a real listing_id, never for wall_art or before publish).

**For Scott:** open COLOR1003's review card and tap "📸 Stage listing photos from pack", then approve the resulting photos in Approvals.

## 2026-07-25 — Full code audit sweep: 9 bugs fixed across the recurring classes (Scott: "Check all of franks code")

Two thorough scans across the full in-scope surface (~47k lines) hunted the bug classes this week already produced three incidents of (ephemeral-path durability, wrong file resolver, runtime writes to git-tracked files, swallowed errors, blocking work in async routes). Findings and fixes, triage order:

**P0 (was actively broken in production):** `tools/video_generator.py` and `tools/ai_video.py` wrote generated videos to the hardcoded ephemeral repo dir, while commit f6a78c7 had moved the READ side (`_FILE_ROOTS["videos"]`: Studio list, Instagram/Facebook posting) to the durable volume — so on the hosted deploy a generated video never appeared in the Studio sidebar and social posting 404'd on it. Both write sides now resolve via the identical HUB_FILES_DIR-or-/data detection main.py uses (and `ai_video.py`'s path is now repo-anchored instead of cwd-relative). Regression test asserts write == read path *exactly*, not just volume-nesting.

**P1:** `tools/post_scheduled_art.py` wrote scheduler state (next_post_date/subjects_used/post_history) back to the git-tracked `data/art_schedule.json` — every redeploy reset it to the committed June values, so the daily art scheduler would think it was overdue and regenerate already-used subjects (duplicate-listing risk). Now resolved via `db.resolve_persistent_path(..., seed_from=...)`, which migrates the committed state to the volume on first run.

**P2:** `tools/build_coloring_product.py` and `tools/build_wallart_product.py` computed the QC verdict as PASS when `qc_sweep.sweep()` matched zero files — so a failed generation logged `DONE: pages=✗ qc=PASS` (the exact false-PASS failure mode build_coloring_product's own docstring warns about, via the empty-rows path its guard missed). Zero rows now reports "NOT CHECKED", never PASS.

**P3:** `tools/trash.py`'s vault was the hardcoded repo dir — on Railway, runtime archives (main.py archiving a deleted todo/allowed-folder, the SOLE copy between delete and restore) vanished on redeploy, silently defeating the "nothing deleted is unrecoverable" guarantee. Vault now resolves to the volume on the hosted runtime; local repo behavior (committed vault, CLAUDE.md's model) unchanged.

**P4:** `tools/shop_health_check.py` wrote the hero-image hash baseline to the git-tracked manifest inside `except Exception: pass` — on Railway the baseline reset every redeploy, producing recurring false "hero has changed" warnings (or silence about a real change), and a failed write was invisible. Now durable via `resolve_persistent_path` with seeding, and a write failure prints a visible warning.

**P5:** Event-loop hygiene in `main.py`: `studio_list_videos`'s glob+stat, `stage_photo`/`stage_video`'s up-to-30MB synchronous writes (and rollback unlinks), plus minor mkdir/stat/write_text in three studio routes, all moved off the event loop via the established `_scan()`/`_write()`+`to_thread` shape. Dated comments added at the two `asyncio.run(_stage_photo_action)` sites explaining exactly why they're safe today and what would break them.

**P6:** `_validate_staged_action`'s create_listing at-approval re-check was the last caller still passing the old prefix-only `_product_file_exists` (harmless today — only listing_id is read off the result — but the same landmine class as COLOR1003). Switched to `_catalog_file_exists`; that bug class is now fully closed.

**Found but deliberately not fixed (follow-up candidates for Scott):** test-coverage gaps — the relay/WebSocket subsystem (biggest; it executes commands on Scott's machine), voice endpoints, studio/social routes, auth admin surface; ~20k lines of orphaned tools/*.py (led by art_creation_tools.py at 5,178 lines) that could be archived; minor accepted noise (listing_manifest.json stamps, review_batches/ reports, tracked image_cache/ JPGs, _zip_entries returning [] for a corrupt ZIP).

**Verification:** new `tests/test_audit_sweep_fixes.py` (12 tests, one literal regression per finding, including first-ever coverage for the stage-photo and studio-videos routes). Full suite 80/80 passed, 3x clean Playwright.

## 2026-07-25 — tools/*.py orphan cleanup: only 1 of ~20 flagged files was real

Following the full code audit, Scott asked to clean up the ~20,000 lines of
`tools/*.py` the audit's inventory scan had flagged as orphaned (led by
`art_creation_tools.py`, 5,178 lines). That scan only checked for direct
`import`/`subprocess` hits inside `main.py`, which misses transitive imports
(a script reached only through another script `main.py` does invoke), CI
workflow-only invocation, and documented manual/operator entrypoints
(CLAUDE.md prose, runtime error messages) — the same blind spot that
already produced 3 false positives elsewhere this session
(`playwright_smoke.py`, `rollback.py`, `build_wallart_product.py`, all
confirmed in active use).

A dedicated re-verification pass checked every file directly under `tools/`
against `main.py`, cross-references from other `tools/*.py` files,
CLAUDE.md, all 4 CI workflow files, `tests/*.py`, and this runbook's own
2026-07-11 decluttering history (which already documents one file,
`gen_room_library.py`, that was trashed and then explicitly restored after
being wrongly judged orphaned).

**Result: only `tools/health_check.py` (372 lines) was genuinely orphaned** —
zero references anywhere, superseded by `shop_health_check.py` (which IS
wired into `_EXEC_COMMANDS` and CLAUDE.md's automation table) plus main.py's
own built-in health loop. Archived via `tools/trash.py` (`archive_file()`,
id `20260725-001`), fully recoverable via
`python tools/trash.py --restore 20260725-001`.

Everything else the scan flagged — including `art_creation_tools.py` itself
— turned out to have a real, verifiable reference once transitive imports
were traced (`art_creation_tools.py` ← `build_wallart_product.py:69` ←
`main.py:11131` subprocess call). 9 further files were flagged AMBIGUOUS
(a real but only-transitive reference through an already-dead file, or a
possibly-still-manual workflow tool) and deliberately left untouched pending
Scott's explicit go-ahead per file: `gen_room_library.py`,
`competitor_intel.py`, `etsy_listing_tools.py`, `fetch_market_examples.py`,
`pinterest_batch_poster.py`, `pinterest_post_queue.py`,
`gen_lifestyle_scene.py`, `gen_sticker_listing_photos.py`,
`approve_listing.py`.

**Lesson for future cleanup sweeps:** a naive `main.py`-only reference scan
is not a safe basis for deletion in this codebase — always trace transitive
imports through other `tools/*.py` files and check CI workflows + CLAUDE.md
prose before archiving anything flagged as "orphaned."

## 2026-07-26 — SKU + category (taxonomy_id) backfill across every Etsy listing

Scott: "I need every listing on Etsy to be categorized and have skus so we
can track everything better." Before this, SKU had zero infrastructure
anywhere (nothing in `EtsyAPIClient`, `product_catalog.json`, or listing
creation ever touched it), and category (`taxonomy_id`) coverage was
partial — only 3 of ~10 categories had a hardcoded default, and even the
existing self-correcting live-check (`_resolve_category_taxonomy_id()`)
only ran for categories that already had a guess in the dict, skipping
exactly the categories that needed it most.

**Two real bugs fixed in `_resolve_category_taxonomy_id()` along the way**
(main.py ~11740): (1) it never attempted the live-listing verification for
a category with no hardcoded default at all — broadened so any category
with ≥1 live listing gets checked/discovered, not just ones already in
`_PRODUCT_TAXONOMY_BY_CATEGORY`. (2) `_CATEGORY_TAXONOMY_VERIFIED` only
cached "did we check," not the resolved value — meaning a live-discovered
correction applied to exactly one call, then reverted to the stale
hardcoded default on every subsequent call in the same process. Now caches
the actual resolved value.

**Shipped:**
- New `update_sku_and_category` staged-action type (main.py
  `_execute_staged_action`) — one combined `update_listing` PATCH when both
  fields need fixing, not two, to minimize edit-count/ranking-signal cost
  per listing (CLAUDE.md Ranking Recovery Playbook). Wired into both
  allowed-type sets, the `stage_action` chat tool, and
  `db._RANKING_RECOVERY_TYPES` (a sku/taxonomy edit resets the same
  ~2-3-week re-index recovery window a tags/title/description edit does).
- Durable work queue (`sku_taxonomy_backfill_queue.json`, volume-or-local
  sidecar) + new weekly loop `_sku_taxonomy_backfill_loop()`
  (`base_interval=604_800`) staging up to 18 fixes/week — the pacing Scott
  approved (~15-20/week) so a ~170-listing sweep doesn't compound-edit the
  whole shop's search ranking at once. Staging makes no Etsy calls and
  carries no ranking risk; only Scott's own approval actually edits a
  listing, so this controls how many NEW actions appear per week, not
  approval itself.
- `stage_product_publish()` now sets `sku` = `product_id` on every new
  listing at creation time, so this never needs a backfill again going
  forward.
- `check_attributes()` (`tools/listing_integrity_check.py`) gained a SKU
  WARN check alongside the existing taxonomy_id WARN — the standing
  guardrail that catches drift after the one-time sweep completes. Only
  checked when a listing maps to exactly one `dp_code` (ambiguous for
  bundles, skipped rather than guessed).
- SKU convention: reuse `product_catalog.json`'s existing `product_id` as
  the SKU verbatim (Scott's choice) — no new catalog field, no renaming of
  the inconsistent/verbose existing product_ids.

**13 `uncategorized` catalog entries** (`MISC_*` product_ids, all
`etsy_sync`-imported, never assigned a category) were inspected and are all
unambiguously `wall_art` — every one's name says "Art Print... Wall
Decor... Multiple Sizes," every file is a `DP####_print_sizes.zip` (the
documented wall-art print-ZIP convention), and every price matches wall-art
tiers. Proposed to Scott directly rather than auto-applied; excluded from
the automatic weekly queue until he confirms.

## 2026-07-29 — Verified Antigravity's static audit of frank_hud_mockup.py; 1 real fix, 1 false positive, 1 overstated finding closed out

Scott set up Google Antigravity (a separate agentic coding tool, Gemini-3-
based) as a second pass on Frank's frontend. Its browser/Playwright install
failed in its own sandbox (404 on the driver download, unrelated to this
repo), so it fell back to a static code audit of `frank_hud_mockup.py` and
reported 3 WARN findings. Each was independently verified against the real
file before acting — consistent with how every finding gets handled in this
codebase, whether it comes from a scan I ran or a different tool entirely.

- **False positive, no action:** claimed `function frame()` was defined
  twice with "the second overwriting the first in global scope." The first
  (line ~3136) is nested *inside* `_animateCountUp()` — a locally-scoped
  function, not global. The second (line ~10283) is the separate, genuinely
  global orb 2D-canvas animation loop. JS scoping keeps these fully
  separate; no collision exists. The static scanner matched same-name-
  anywhere-in-file without checking nesting depth.
- **Overstated, no action:** claimed 202 hardcoded hex colors should be
  theme variables. This file defines 10+ complete theme palettes (each
  `[data-theme]` block redefines `--cyan`/`--gold`/etc.), so grepped for
  CSS rules mixing `var(--...)` with a raw hex in the same declaration to
  find the real pattern behind most matches: `background:var(--gold);
  color:#0D1B2A` (and the --cyan/--green/--red equivalents) repeated across
  dozens of buttons — a deliberate, correct contrast pattern (bright accent
  background + fixed near-black text that stays readable against every
  theme's accent hue), not a theme-inconsistency bug. Forcing these into
  variables would risk breaking contrast in themes where the accent is
  itself dark.
- **Real, fixed:** "17/131 buttons have `aria-label`" (independently
  recounted as 17/129 — matches). Most of the other buttons already have
  real visible text serving as their accessible name and don't need one.
  After filtering to genuinely icon-only buttons with zero accessible name,
  exactly 2 gaps existed: `.refimg-del` (×, had only an unreliable `title`
  attr) and the to-do delete button (✕, had nothing). Both fixed with
  `aria-label`.

Lesson for future cross-tool audits: treat a second AI tool's findings the
same as any other unverified input — confirm against the real file before
acting, the same discipline already applied to this session's own scans.
A naive static scanner especially cannot reason about JS scope nesting or
a file's own multi-theme CSS architecture.

## 2026-07-29 — Desktop layout: reclaimed a whole empty column, fixed nav dead-zone, widened chat

Scott sent a photo of Frank's desktop view: "too much unused space... make
the chat actually able to be used." Investigation (research pass +
follow-up questions confirming this was visual/cramped, not a functional
bug) found the real causes, all in `tools/api_server/frank_hud_mockup.py`:

1. **The single biggest cause, found only by reading the CSS carefully**:
   `.col-left` (a fixed 290px column on the Home/chat screen) contains
   three panels — AI Core Overview, Dependency Health, Mission Timeline —
   that are ALL hidden by default via `body:not(.show-plumbing)` (from the
   2026-07-01 "hide plumbing" redesign, task #18). For a normal user (not
   in dev mode), that left a fully empty 290px-wide column doing nothing
   for the entire height of the screen. A prior research pass on this same
   layout (earlier this session) missed this — it described `.col-left`'s
   contents as visible, real content, without checking the `show-plumbing`
   gate. Fixed by hiding the whole column (not just its children) and
   collapsing `.main`'s grid from `290px 1fr 310px` to `1fr 310px` for
   normal users — chat reclaims the full 290px + gap. `show-plumbing` dev
   mode keeps the original 3-column layout unchanged.
2. `fitStage()`'s size ceiling (`STAGE_W_MAX`/`STAGE_H_MAX`) was 1920×1200
   — a below-average size for monitors sold today. Above that, the app
   stopped growing its real layout and just `transform:scale()`d the fixed
   stage, producing symmetric letterboxing on any wider monitor. Raised to
   2560×1440 (QHD, very common) so real layout content fills up to that
   size instead of letterboxing; a true ultrawide (3440px+) still gets some
   letterboxing above that, which is the original, still-valid "don't let
   the content column get absurdly wide" intent, just at a much higher bar.
   Note: this ceiling had already been silently raised once before, from
   1800×1000 to 1920×1200, in commit `8078d7a` (2026-07-26) — that change
   had no matching ops_runbook entry, flagging here for the record since
   this entry builds on top of it.
3. The left nav rail's "Quick Commands" block used `margin-top:auto`,
   shoving it to the very bottom of a now-taller (up to 1440px) sidebar —
   a large dead gap between the short nav list and the buttons. Changed to
   a fixed `margin-top:20px` so it sits close to the nav list.
4. Chat bubble `max-width` raised from 78% to 85% now that the chat column
   is significantly wider, so less of that new width reads as blank margin
   beside every message.

Verified visually via real Playwright screenshots at 1920×1080, 2560×1440,
1440×900 (floor), and 3440×1440 (ultrawide) — confirmed no letterboxing up
to 2560×1440, no dead gap above Quick Commands, and chat visibly wider.
Also screenshotted Products/Approvals/Files (other desktop screens, which
don't share this 3-column shell) to confirm no analogous issue elsewhere —
none found; those screens were already using their available width well.

Lesson: a CSS-reading research pass can still miss the actual root cause
if it doesn't check every conditional-visibility rule (`show-plumbing`,
`show-advanced`) touching the elements in question — worth explicitly
checking display:none gates on anything that "looks like real content" in
a static read, not just describing what the markup contains.

## 2026-07-29 — Desktop content-cutoff bug (Scott: "chat is still cut off / section to the right") — real root cause found and fixed, closes task #289
**Symptom:** On Scott's real laptop browser window (~1366×672, well under the app's STAGE_H_MIN=900 floor), the COGS & Profit card's disclaimer text trailed off at the bottom edge and the Inbox & Reviews card was not visible at all — genuine, silent content clipping, not a rendering glitch. Scott's framing ("there has to be a way to auto detect the screen setting... it should auto adjust") suggested a missing detection mechanism, but the resize listener + `fitStage()` clamp-and-scale mechanism already existed and fired correctly — the bug was in what that mechanism produced, a CSS Grid sizing defect, not a missing trigger.

**Why this survived 3 prior "Desktop layout fix" passes (`8078d7a`, `98ad5ef`, `aab770f`):** every one of them verified only at-or-above the 900px floor (1440×900 and up). The bug only reproduces below the floor, on a real laptop viewport, which none of them ever tested.

**Real root cause (found via direct DOM measurement, not guessed) — two-part chain:**
1. `#stage{display:grid;grid-template-rows:68px 1fr 54px}` — the middle row was a bare `1fr`. A bare `fr` track has an *implicit automatic minimum* equal to its content's min-content size, which silently overrides `min-height:0` set on the grid item inside it. Fixed: `68px minmax(0,1fr) 54px`.
2. `.main` (the 3-column chat layout: left panel / chat / right panel) is **not** a direct grid item of `#stage` despite having `grid-column:2;grid-row:2` — its real parent is `#screen-cmd` (a `.screen` div), and `.screen.active{display:block}` is a plain block box, not a grid container, so `.main`'s own grid-placement properties are inert no-ops. `#screen-cmd` (the actual grid item) already sized correctly to 778px after fix #1 + `.screen{min-height:0}`, but `.main`, as an ordinary block child with no explicit height, just grew to its own content's natural size (914px) and silently overflowed its already-correctly-sized parent. Since `#stage-wrap{position:fixed;inset:0}` has no ancestor to scroll, that overflow was clipped at the literal browser window edge with no scrollbar reachable anywhere. Fixed: `.main{height:100%}`.

Also fixed as defense-in-depth: `.panel.col-agents`/`.panel.col-feed{min-height:140px}` (was losing to `.panel{min-height:0}` via a same-specificity cascade tie resolved by source order — switched to compound selectors), and `#inbox-body` given the `panel-body` class so it has its own working internal scroll like `#feed-list` already did.

**Verification:** every fix step was measured directly in a real browser (`clientHeight`/`scrollHeight`/`getComputedStyle`) at a real 1366×672 viewport with realistic injected card content (this dev environment has no live Etsy/Anthropic creds, so cards normally stay in a short placeholder state that doesn't reproduce the real content density from Scott's screenshot) before being written into the source file. New regression test added to `tools/playwright_smoke.py` that specifically exercises the sub-floor viewport class every prior pass missed — asserts `.col-right`'s `overflow-y:auto` genuinely engages (`scrollHeight > clientHeight`) and that Inbox & Reviews keeps a real non-zero height, so this exact bug class can't silently regress a 4th time.

**Files:** `tools/api_server/frank_hud_mockup.py` (`#stage` grid-template-rows, `.screen{min-height:0}`, `.main{height:100%}`, `.panel.col-agents`/`.panel.col-feed`, `#inbox-body` markup), `tools/playwright_smoke.py` (new sub-floor regression block). Build `abd7f0b-v267`.

## 2026-07-29 (later) — Bambu P1S printer monitoring added to Frank

Scott pasted an "Implementation Plan" for wiring the Bambu Lab P1S into "Frank Command Center" (Access Code + serial included in the message). Investigated before building anything: the plan targeted `command_center.py` at repo root — a separate, older Flask tool that only runs locally at `localhost:5055` — not the actual Frank dashboard (`tools/api_server/main.py` + `frank_hud_mockup.py`) Scott uses remotely, which is deployed to Railway with no route to his home LAN. Asked Scott directly which he wanted; he chose the real Frank via a local bridge, the same shape as the existing `frank_relay.py` pattern (a small process on Scott's own network that reports up to the cloud service, rather than the cloud service reaching down to the LAN).

**Shipped:**
- `main.py`: in-memory printer state (`_printer_telemetry`/`_printer_frame`, same tradeoff as `_relay_ws` — a redeploy just means "bridge offline" until the next push, no durability needed for live device state) + 4 endpoints: `POST /api/printer/telemetry`, `GET /api/printer/status` (reports `online:false` whenever nothing's been pushed in the last 30s — never presents stale numbers as live), `POST /api/printer/camera-frame`, `GET /api/printer/camera.jpg` (404s past the same 30s staleness window, same honesty rule).
- `tools/relay/bambu_p1s_bridge.py` (new) + `tools/relay/bambu_requirements.txt` (`paho-mqtt`): standalone script, same deployment shape as `frank_relay.py`, connects to the P1S over local MQTT (port 8883, `bblp`/Access Code auth, self-signed cert — same tradeoff every open-source Bambu LAN integration makes), parses `gcode_state`/temps/progress/layers/AMS/HMS from the printer's `print` report, pushes to Frank via authenticated HTTP POST. `--test` verifies the MQTT handshake standalone.
- **Caught and fixed a real integrity problem before shipping it**: the first draft of the camera-relay code included a fabricated binary auth-packet layout (invented magic bytes presented as if they were documented protocol constants) for the P1S's local camera stream, which Bambu Lab has never publicly documented. Sending fabricated bytes to a raw socket on Scott's real printer with no way to verify correctness would have been worse than not building it. Removed the fabricated implementation entirely — camera relay ships as an explicit, honest "not implemented" stub (`--test-camera` explains why) rather than code dressed up as more certain than it is. Telemetry (well-documented across the open-source Bambu ecosystem) shipped at full confidence; the receiving endpoints (`camera-frame`/`camera.jpg`) are already in place for whenever the protocol is actually confirmed.
- `frank_hud_mockup.py`: new "🖨️ Bambu P1S Printer" card on Home (`col-meminsights`, same visual pattern as Star Seller/Ads/COGS), `loadPrinterStatus()` wired into `_SCREEN_LOADERS.cmd`. Shows state badge, progress bar, layer count, ETA, nozzle/bed/chamber temps, speed mode, AMS tray color chips; shows an honest "BRIDGE OFFLINE" state with setup instructions when nothing's reporting (true today — no bridge has been run against real hardware yet).
- New `tests/test_printer_telemetry.py` (8 cases: roundtrip, offline-before-first-report, stale-data-reports-offline, camera roundtrip, missing/stale camera 404s, oversized-frame 413 + never stored). `tools/playwright_smoke.py` extended to confirm the card renders the offline state cleanly in CI (no bridge there either).
- `CLAUDE.md`: new "Bambu P1S Live Monitoring (Frank Integration)" section with the real setup steps (env vars, `.env` location, `--test` flag) and the camera caveat.

**Not done / explicitly deferred:** camera relay (see above — needs the real protocol confirmed against hardware, or Scott pointing the bridge at a known-working reference implementation). No hard-coded credentials anywhere in the diff — Access Code/IP/serial live only in `tools/relay/.env` (gitignored, same file `frank_relay.py` already uses), which Scott fills in on his own machine. Build `4ec5e9a-v268`.

## 2026-07-30 — command_center.py audit: 4 reported issues verified + 2 severe undiscovered bugs found and fixed

Scott pasted an audit plan listing 4 issues in `command_center.py`. Verified each against the real code before touching anything (2 confirmed real, verified fixes applied to command_center.py; 2 low-severity SyntaxWarning claims confirmed real too and fixed) — but while verifying, direct JS-syntax checking of the rendered templates surfaced two much more severe, previously-undiscovered bugs, one of which was live-broken in production.

**Confirmed from the original 4 items:**
1. `python3` hardcoded instead of the running interpreter — real. `cmd_args[0]` now normalized to `sys.executable` when it's `python3`/`python`/`./venv/bin/python3`/`./venv/bin/python`, in both `command_center.py`'s own `run_command()` (local standalone use) and `main.py`'s separate, near-duplicate `api_run_command()` (the one actually serving the Railway-hosted `/cmd` page).
2. `onclick="runCmd('{{ cmd.label | replace(\"'\", \"\\'\") }}', ...)"` — real quote-escaping bug (the `replace` was a no-op inside Jinja2, `\'` there is just `'`). Fixed by switching to `data-cmd-id`/`data-cmd-label` HTML attributes read via `.dataset` in JS — correct because Jinja2's HTML autoescaping (already on by default) is what actually protects an HTML attribute value, not hand-rolled JS-string escaping. Verified: `render_template_string('<div data-x="{{ v }}">', v="it's a test")` → `it&#39;s a test`. No current command label contains an apostrophe (checked all 28), so this was latent, not yet triggered.
3. `os.read(fd, 4096).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")` corrupting multibyte UTF-8 split across reads — real. Replaced with a `codecs.getincrementaldecoder("utf-8")()` per fd in both `command_center.py` and `main.py`'s copy.
4. Invalid escape sequences (`\d`, `\$`) causing `SyntaxWarning` — real, reproduced with `python3 -W error`. Fixed `generate_print_sizes.py`'s module docstring (converted to raw string, pure text, no risk) and 5 exact JS-regex-literal spots in `frank_hud_mockup.py`'s giant HTML/JS string (doubled the backslash at each site rather than converting the whole 10k-line non-f-string template to raw, since it legitimately uses other Python escapes elsewhere and a blanket conversion risked silently changing unrelated behavior).

**Found and fixed, NOT in the original list — the real severity here:**
- **`command_center.py`'s `HTML` template had a live JS-breaking bug of the exact class already documented once before in this repo** (`test_frank_hud_js_syntax.py`, 2026-07-22, for `frank_hud_mockup.py`): a literal `\n` typed directly into a non-raw Python triple-quoted string gets silently decoded by Python into a real embedded newline *inside* a JS single-quoted string literal, which is illegal JS syntax and kills the entire `<script>` block. Two instances: `clearOutput()`'s "Console cleared." span, and `runCmd()`'s "Initializing task" span. This meant **the Command Center's entire client-side JS (theme switching, clock, search, keyboard shortcuts, command execution — everything in that one `<script>` block) was non-functional in any real browser**, confirmed by extracting the actual post-import string and running `node --check` on it (reproduced the exact failure both before and after each fix). Fixed both (`\n` → `\\n` so Python's escape resolution produces a literal 2-char `\n` in the JS output, which JS then correctly interprets at its own level). New regression test `tests/test_command_center_js_syntax.py`, mirroring the existing `frank_hud_mockup.py` test — command_center.py had no equivalent coverage before, which is exactly why this regressed silently.
- **`main.py`'s `api_run_command()` (the actual `/run` handler behind the Railway-hosted `/cmd` page) was missing `import shlex` entirely** — `shlex` is used at `cmd_args = shlex.split(cmd)` but never imported anywhere in the 15k-line file. Every single click of "Execute" on any Command Center button on the live, deployed Frank has been throwing `NameError: name 'shlex' is not defined` this whole time. Fixed with one import line. New test `tests/test_api_run_command_fixes.py` (also covers the sys.executable/UTF-8-decoder fixes applied to this same route) calls the real route function end-to-end (draining its async `body_iterator`) and would have caught this on the first run.

**Files:** `command_center.py` (imports, `run_command()`'s `generate()`, button template, `runCmd()`, `clearOutput()`, `runCmd()`'s Initializing-task line), `tools/api_server/main.py` (imports — `shlex` added, `codecs` added — `api_run_command()`'s `generate()`), `tools/generate_print_sizes.py` (docstring), `tools/api_server/frank_hud_mockup.py` (5 regex-literal backslash fixes). New tests: `tests/test_command_center_js_syntax.py`, `tests/test_command_center_fixes.py`, `tests/test_api_run_command_fixes.py`. Build `2c8be37-v269`.

## 2026-07-30 (later) — Frank Phone/HUD plan: 3 of 4 "bug" claims didn't hold up, 1 real autofill nuisance fixed

Scott pasted a follow-up plan bundling three things: (1) a re-proposal of P1S monitoring via `command_center.py` + a new `/printer` route — already shipped the prior evening via the correct architecture (local bridge → Frank, see 2026-07-29's entry); (2) the same 4 command_center.py audit items already fixed hours earlier in this session; (3) four new Frank Phone/HUD "bug fixes." Investigated (3) before touching anything, same as every other claim this session:

- **"`value="Sjack7"` pre-fill on `#chat-input`"** — false. No such attribute exists anywhere in `frank_hud_mockup.py`; the input is `placeholder`-only. "Sjack7" is Scott's real local OS username (confirmed from his own terminal). The far more likely explanation: the login page's real username field (`name="username" autocomplete="username"`, same origin) has a saved credential, and the browser's autofill heuristics are suggesting it into an unrelated same-origin text field — a browser behavior, not a server bug.
- **"Null pointer in Quick Commands' `+ Start New Task`"** — false. `showScreen()` is a synchronous CSS-class toggle (verified by reading it); `#hud-todo-input` is static markup always present in the DOM, just hidden via `.screen:not(.active){display:none}`. The claimed `document.getElementById('hud-todo-input')` call in that onclick can never see `null`.
- **"Missing mic permission toast"** — false. `toggleVoiceCapture()` already catches `getUserMedia()` rejection and shows `⚠️ Microphone access denied or unavailable` as a bot chat bubble.
- **"Missing OAuth re-auth prompt on Health Check"** — false. Already extensive: a dedicated "🔧 System health" section in Approvals separates token/infra issues from content issues (2026-07-18), proactive staleness warnings fire before the 90-day refresh token actually expires, and every failure message names the exact remediation command (`python tools/etsy_oauth.py`).

**Applied anyway** (real, low-risk, addresses the likely actual cause of the Sjack7 symptom): added `name="chat-message"` to `#chat-input` — an explicit, non-username-like name gives the browser's autofill heuristic a clean signal instead of falling back to less predictable matching when no `name` is present at all.

**Not started — needs explicit scope confirmation, not silently bundled into a "bug fix" plan:** the plan's "Visual Styling & Contrast Overhaul" (glassmorphism chat input, bubble recolor, sidebar typography/padding, responsive auto-collapse) is real, substantial, subjective design work — same category as every other visual redesign this session, which all shipped only after screenshots and explicit sign-off, not as a byproduct of a bug-fix pass.

**Files:** `tools/api_server/frank_hud_mockup.py` (`#chat-input`'s `name` attribute only). Build `55ffd0a-v270`.

## 2026-07-30 (later still) — Frank Phone/HUD visual redesign: input glass, bubble contrast, sidebar readability

Shipped the 4-item visual overhaul Scott asked for after the audit fixes, per the plan approved and executed this session. Verified all 4 with real Playwright screenshots (default dark theme + the built-in light theme, since the input-box complaint was theme-dependent) before shipping, matching this session's standard practice for subjective visual work.

1. **Chat input** — was `background:var(--panel2)`, which is genuinely near-white on the light theme and several pastel themes (confirmed: `--panel2:#dde4ec` on light, `#ffeee0`/`#f5ebd0` on two pastel themes). Switched to `rgba(0,0,0,.28)` + `backdrop-filter:blur(10px)` — a consistent dark glass pane regardless of active theme — plus a gold-border + cyan-glow `:focus` state (`box-shadow:0 0 0 1px var(--gold),0 0 14px rgba(96,220,255,.35)`) layered onto the existing `border-color:var(--gold)` focus rule rather than replacing it.
2. **Chat bubbles** — user bubbles were a flat `var(--gold)` fill (confirmed genuinely orange/amber in most themes: `#e4b155`, `#f7b731`, `#f5b878`...). Changed to mirror the bot bubble's own existing pattern (accent border on a `--panel2` glass background) instead of a solid fill — `border:1px solid var(--gold);border-right-width:3px` — so user and bot bubbles now read as a matched pair using the same gold/cyan branding with less visual weight.
3. **Sidebar cards** (`.ss-row`/`.ss-status` — shared by Star Seller, Ads & ROAS, COGS & Profit, and the new Printer card) — font-size raised 11px→13px (12px for the status badge), row padding 4px→6px. Deliberately scoped to these two classes rather than the shared `.panel` container, which is also used by unrelated panels (chat, left-column system health) this wasn't about.
4. **Responsive collapse** — investigated before writing any code, per the plan's own "verify before building" directive. Screenshots at 1024/900/700px confirmed the desktop 3-column HUD already scales cleanly down to ~880px via the existing `fitStage()` mechanism, and below that it switches to Frank's entirely separate, purpose-built mobile phone UI (`.screen`-based app-launcher home) — not a squished desktop layout. No new work was needed; this item is already correctly handled by existing code.

**Files:** `tools/api_server/frank_hud_mockup.py` (`#chat-input`/`:focus`, `.lc-bubble.user`, `.ss-status`/`.ss-row`). Build `c9fcbf4-v271`.

## 2026-07-30 — P1S card: staleness-flicker fix + click-through camera feed
**Symptom (Scott):** "I would like to click on it and see the camera feed. I also need all the stats about the printer live. They keep going away and random info pops up."

**Root cause of the flicker:** `_PRINTER_STALE_SECS` (backend "is this bridge data live" cutoff) was 30s and the HUD's global refresh (`setInterval(loadAll, 30000)`) was also exactly 30s -- zero margin between them. Any single missed poll (network jitter, a backgrounded tab getting its timers throttled, one slow Railway request) flipped the card to "BRIDGE OFFLINE" even though `bambu_p1s_bridge.py` was still pushing telemetry every ~3s.

**Fix:**
- `_PRINTER_STALE_SECS` raised 30s -> 90s (main.py); added a separate `_PRINTER_CAMERA_STALE_SECS = 15` since camera frames arrive far more often than telemetry once connected, so a stuck camera relay should surface faster than a stuck telemetry push.
- Added a dedicated 5s `setInterval` for `loadPrinterStatus()` (only while the Home/`cmd` screen and tab are visible), independent of the 30s global `loadAll()` cycle -- the numbers now actually refresh every 5s instead of every 30s.
- Camera relay implemented in `bambu_p1s_bridge.py` (previously a deliberate "NOT IMPLEMENTED" stub -- the P1S's local camera port 6000 has never been officially documented by Bambu Lab, so no protocol bytes were guessed). Independently verified the real protocol shape by fetching and reading the actual source of `coelacant1/Bambu-Lab-Cloud-API` (GPLv3) directly -- not copied (GPLv3 is incompatible with this codebase), reimplemented from the underlying (non-copyrightable) protocol facts: an 80-byte TLS auth packet, then a 16-byte little-endian frame header + JPEG payload per frame. Runs as a background thread alongside telemetry by default; `--no-camera` disables it, `--test-camera` smoke-tests the connection alone. paho-mqtt import moved lazy (inside `_build_client()`) so the camera-only path, and anything testing the module's pure functions, doesn't need it installed.
- P1S panel-title is now clickable (`openPrinterDetailModal()`), opening the existing generic `#metric-detail-modal` shell with full live stats plus `<img src="/api/printer/camera.jpg?...">`, refreshed every 5s while open; falls back to an honest "no camera signal yet" / "bridge offline" message rather than showing a stale frame.

**Caveat told to Scott:** the camera protocol is best-effort/unofficial (never Bambu-documented) -- `--test-camera` on the actual bridge machine is the way to confirm it works against the real printer; this sandbox has no way to test against real hardware.

**Verified:** `tests/test_printer_telemetry.py` (staleness split), new `tests/test_bambu_p1s_bridge.py` (camera auth-packet byte layout against the verified spec, frame-reader desync/oversize handling -- runs without paho-mqtt installed, matching CI), `tools/playwright_smoke.py` click-through-modal coverage (3x clean). Build `0509ec4-v272`.

## 2026-07-30 — HUD transition/animation durations trimmed for a snappier feel
**Symptom (Scott):** "Make sure everything is running as fast as you possibly can. I need very smooth transitions. No delay when doing any action. Anything clicked is as instant as possible."

**Investigation before touching anything:** audited the click-response path end to end looking for a real blocking bug (the same discipline as the P1S staleness fix earlier today) -- `showScreen()` is fully synchronous (class toggles only, screen loaders fire-and-forget after), `approveAction()`/`bulkApproveLowRisk()` show a spinner synchronously before the network call (can't be instant for a real Etsy write -- has to wait for the real result), `sendMsg()` adds the user's own chat bubble to the DOM before the WS round-trip, and the orb's WebGL render loop already skips rendering whenever the dashboard (`cc-open`) is showing (2026-07-08 perf pass) so it isn't competing with dashboard clicks for the main thread. No hidden blocking bug found this time, unlike the P1S case.

**What was actually slow:** the UI's own CSS transition/animation durations were longer than they needed to be for a "snappy" feel -- all GPU-accelerated (opacity/transform only, confirmed no layout-triggering properties), just dialed conservatively. Trimmed by ~35-40% across the board:
- Screen switches + phone panel opens (`screen-in`): 260ms -> 150ms
- Chat bubble entrance (`bubble-in`): 220ms -> 140ms
- Product-review modal open/close (`prm-in`): 240ms/180ms -> 150ms/120ms
- Metric-detail modal open/close (`mdm-in`): 240ms/180ms -> 150ms/120ms
- Toast in/out: 180ms -> 120ms

Every JS `setTimeout` that has to stay in lockstep with a closing animation (removing the `-closing` class, removing a toast element from the DOM) was updated to match the new shorter durations -- these pairs must move together or the class gets removed before/after the animation actually finishes, causing a visible glitch.

**Verified:** `tests/test_frank_hud_js_syntax.py`, full suite (87/87), `tools/playwright_smoke.py` 3x clean (one unrelated transient flake on the first attempt -- a Three.js asset fetch race in this sandbox's headless Chromium, unrelated to this diff, reproduced-gone on immediate rerun). Build `7c3dcde-v273`.

## 2026-07-30 — Frank couldn't identify a pasted listing ID/product code
**Symptom (Scott):** "I just put a listing id in his chat. He didn't know what the product was."

**Root cause:** the only ID-lookup tool Frank had (`get_listing`) queries Etsy directly by numeric listing_id and silently fails on anything else -- but this shop's own product catalog identifies things by internal product code (DP1026, SS1001, WA1030, CB001, etc. -- see CLAUDE.md's Product Catalog / SKU Naming Convention sections), not raw Etsy IDs. If Scott pasted a product code, or any identifier that isn't a bare digit string, `get_listing`'s `int(lid)` call raised and the bare `except Exception` swallowed it into a generic "not found" -- Frank was never wrong to say he didn't know, the tool genuinely couldn't answer that shape of input.

**Fix:** new `get_product` agent tool + `_resolve_product()` helper (main.py). Cross-references `data/product_catalog.json` (the shop's real source of truth) by internal product_id, by numeric listing_id via the catalog's `etsy_listing_id` field, or by a name-fragment search -- then merges in a live Etsy fetch (title, state, price, views, favorites) when the matched entry has a listing_id. Falls back to a direct Etsy lookup for a numeric ID that isn't catalogued yet (so a brand-new or un-catalogued listing is never reported unknown), and returns disambiguation candidates instead of guessing when a name fragment matches more than one product. Reuses `_build_products_status()` -- the exact function `/api/products` and the Files tab already call -- so it can never disagree with what those screens show.

Also added an explicit "IDENTIFIER LOOKUP" instruction to the system prompt: the moment Scott sends a bare identifier with little context, Frank must call `get_product` before replying, never ask what he means or say he doesn't know without trying it first.

**Verified:** new `tests/test_get_product_tool.py` (internal code, numeric-ID-via-catalog, unique/ambiguous name-fragment, un-catalogued-listing fallback, 404, and a transient-Etsy-failure-still-returns-catalog-data case), `tests/smoke_test.py` (tool registry), full suite (87/87). Build `e985f7a-v274`.

## 2026-07-30 — Chat input stopped accepting text after sending a message
**Symptom (Scott):** "I cannot enter more than one thing into chat. After frank responds I can no longer add to the chat."

**Root cause, reproduced directly (Playwright):** `sendMsg()` never returned focus to the input after sending. Pressing the Enter key naturally leaves focus on the `<input>` (so that path always worked), but clicking the round send button -- the normal way to send on mobile, and a common way on desktop -- moves browser focus onto the `<button>` itself. Nothing ever gave it back. On mobile this also dismisses the on-screen keyboard. Confirmed with a real headless-browser test: after clicking `#chat-send`, `document.activeElement` was the button, and typing afterward (without manually re-clicking the input) landed nowhere -- `#chat-input`'s value stayed empty even though real keydown events were firing. That is the exact bug: send a message by tapping Send, get a response, then be unable to add anything further without first realizing you need to manually tap back into the input.

**Fix:** `sendMsg()` now calls `inp.focus()` at the end, synchronously within the same user-gesture call stack it already runs in (works whether triggered by Enter or a click/tap). Single fix covers all three chat entry points (`#chat-input`, `#orb-chat-input`, `#quick-chat-input`) since `sendQuickChat()`/the orb send button both route through this same function.

**Verified:** new Playwright regression in `tools/playwright_smoke.py` reproducing the exact repro steps (send via click, assert focus returns to the input, type without re-clicking, assert the keystrokes land in the field) -- 3x clean. Full suite 87/87. Build `47b8ad7-v275`.

## 2026-07-30 — CI failure: Products-filter Playwright race (blocked previous deploy)
**Symptom:** the previous push (chat-input focus fix, commit 9832972) passed all 87 unit tests in CI but failed the real-browser Playwright step on 2 unrelated assertions ("filtering to wall_art should show only wall_art products", "a product with a missing file should name it") -- CI gates the Railway deploy, so the fix never went live even though nothing about the actual fix was broken.

**Root cause:** a pre-existing race in `tools/playwright_smoke.py`'s Products-screen block, unrelated to the chat fix. `showScreen('products')` fires the real `loadProducts()`, an async fetch of the real (now 176-product) `/api/products`. The test then stubs a 3-product fixture directly onto the `_products` binding and asserts against it -- but the real fetch can resolve at any point afterward and clobber the stub, since it's a genuinely separate, uncontrolled async operation (reassigning the top-level `loadProducts` function binding afterward, the fix pattern a *later* block in this same file already uses, does NOT retarget it -- `_SCREEN_LOADERS.products` captured the original function reference at page-load, not a live binding). CI's failure output showed the real catalog ("Products — 5/176 have all files present") had landed instead of the 3-item stub -- confirming the real fetch won the race that run. Passed 3/3 locally beforehand purely by luck of local timing.

**Fix:** mock `authGet` for `/api/products` (same pattern already used elsewhere in this file, documented in `.claude/rules/testing.md`) so the real in-flight fetch resolves to the *same* 3-product data as the stub -- the race becomes harmless because both outcomes are now identical, regardless of timing. Restores the real `authGet` afterward.

**Verified:** 3x clean local Playwright runs + full suite (87/87) before re-shipping. Build `9832972-v276`.

## 2026-07-30 — Workflows screen: qc_sweep/listing_integrity_check "ran but nothing was caught"
**Symptom (Scott):** ran qc_sweep and listing_integrity_check from the Workflows screen yesterday — both reported as having run, but showed no findings.

**Root cause:** `_run_exec_command()` (the function backing every Workflows-screen run, the `execute_command` chat tool, and the run_script staged-action path — all 11 registered commands, including `qc_sweep` and `listing_integrity_check`) truncated combined stdout+stderr to the FIRST ~1900 characters. Both scripts print their real verdict LAST — qc_sweep's `RESULT: N FAIL · M WARN · K PASS` line, listing_integrity_check's `SUMMARY:` block — so any run whose output exceeded ~1900 chars had its verdict silently replaced with "[output truncated]" before Scott ever saw it. Confirmed directly: even a small local qc_sweep run (15 files) already produces ~2800 chars, so this wasn't an edge case at Scott's real ~176-product catalog scale — it fired on every real-sized run. A genuine FAIL/WARN always read as a clean pass.

Checked the separate automated weekly quality-audit rotation loop for the same bug — it parses the full untruncated subprocess output before any truncation happens, so it was NOT affected. This was specific to the interactively-triggered Workflows/Command Center path Scott used directly.

**Fix:** `_run_exec_command()` now keeps a head chunk for context plus the FULL final 4000 characters (raised the cap to 12000 total), so the verdict/summary line can never be lost regardless of total output length. Applies uniformly to all registered exec commands (shop_health_check, listing_compliance_sweep, check_digital_file_exposure, etc.) since they share this one function.

**Verified:** new `tests/test_exec_command_output_truncation.py` (short output passes through unchanged, a large fixture with the verdict at the end survives truncation with the verdict intact, head context preserved). Full suite 88/88. Build `454c3db-v277`.

## 2026-07-30 — Fix-anywhere buttons, reference-photo wiring, wall-art art QA (Scott request)
Four changes shipped together, build 68ab3f5-v278:
- **Listings tab:** "Ask Frank to Fix" now shows on every listing row, not just inactive/manifest-FAIL ones (Scott: "I want a button... even if it's already been approved"). Backend `request_listing_fix()` skips staging a `publish_listing` republish action when the listing is already active (was a meaningless no-op PATCH dressed up as an approval).
- **Products tab:** `openProductInfoSheet()` (the dead-end shown for fully-ready/published products) now has a "Ask Frank to fix this" button wired to the existing `/api/conversion-targets/{listing_id}/fix` diagnose-then-stage endpoint.
- **Create screen — image engine dropdowns:** the "Make a listing photo" engine picker was never actually read by `lsgGenerate()` — every click silently generated with gpt-image-1 regardless of selection. Now reads and passes `engine`; `generate_verified_photo()` (listing_photo_pipeline.py) now routes its OpenAI-compatible branch through `image_gen.edit_image()` so gpt-image-2 actually takes effect. Removed Ideogram from that dropdown (edit-style call, Ideogram is generate-only) and added it to `_engineOptionsHtml()` (cover-art/wall-art/coloring-page generators, all pure-generate — backend already allowed it via `_APPROVED_ART_ENGINES`, frontend just never offered it).
- **Reference Photos library:** previously upload-only ("doesn't feed into anything Frank generates yet"). Now: picking a reference image on the Wall Art "+ new one" panel runs one cached vision call (`image_gen.describe_reference_style()`) that turns it into style notes appended to the generation prompt. Scoped to Wall Art only this round — Coloring Pages' description field is subject-line text expanded by an LLM call, not a direct image prompt, so wiring it in needs a different hook point (follow-on).
- **Wall art art quality:** `generate_wall_art_master()` was a single-shot generate-and-hope call with zero automated QA. Now routed through `goal_loop.run_until_goal()` with a new `image_gen.verify_original_art()` vision check (garbled baked-in text, broken collage composition, wrong subject) — up to one retry with the specific failure fed back as corrective prompt text. Never raises on an exhausted QA miss (uses the last attempt, logs a loud warning) — only a real generation error raises. First product-art generator on this pattern; planner covers/sticker sheets/coloring pages are natural follow-ons, not done this round.

Full suite (89/89) + 3x clean playwright_smoke.py before shipping.

## 2026-07-30 — Home-screen UX pass (screen-by-screen audit, page 2, build 63f3837-v279)
Reviewed both Home surfaces (mobile `#screen-home` launcher, desktop `#screen-cmd`
"Command Center") against an adversarial subagent pass before implementing. Two
findings from the draft plan turned out to be false positives once checked against
the real code — recorded here so the same ground isn't re-covered:
- Desktop's `.col-left` (AI Core/Dependency Health/Mission Timeline) is hidden by
  default on purpose — a 2026-07-29 fix for Scott's own "too much unused space"
  report. Left untouched.
- A per-tile keyboard Enter/Space handler was drafted for Home's tiles, then
  reverted — a pre-existing document-level keydown listener (2026-07-08) already
  activates any focused `role="button"` element app-wide. The draft handler
  double-fired every keypress against that existing one; playwright_smoke.py caught
  it before shipping.

Shipped: (1) ticker gets a "Revenue · Today" chip alongside its existing 30d
figures (reused `m.orders.today_revenue`, already fetched by loadShopPerf(), no new
endpoint), (2) personalized time-of-day greeting on the mobile Home hero via the
existing GET /api/me, (3) desktop Inbox & Reviews panel caps its review list to 2
inline with a "N more" expand toggle (same pattern as Shop Performance's existing
expand/collapse — previously the only col-right card with no length limit).

Full suite (89/89) + 3x clean playwright_smoke.py before shipping.

## 2026-07-30 — Home screen: mobile header overflow bug (build aa6a608-v280)
Scott reported live from the shipped Home screen: "the top is not accessible" (a
screenshot showed the desktop header row -- search, Command Center link, bell/help/
gear icons, operator chip -- cut off on both edges of the phone viewport).

Root cause: `.hdr-bar`/`.hdr-logo` were only hidden on mobile under
`body.is-mobile.phone-panel` (the Ask/Approvals/Today/Create/More tab-bar screens,
set by `phoneTab()`). Home is reached via `phoneOpenScreen()` instead, which sets a
different marker (`phone-screen-open`, not `phone-panel`) -- so the full desktop
header rendered at 390px width and overflowed off-screen, unreachable. This affects
every screen reached via `phoneOpenScreen()`, not just Home (Create, Products,
Listings, etc. all use the same path) -- the fix covers all of them at once.

Fix: added the matching hide rule for `body.is-mobile.phone-screen-open`. Verified
live via a one-off Playwright script (mobile 390x844 viewport, real login) before
shipping: `document.documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth` (390 === 390, zero
horizontal overflow) and both header elements confirmed `display:none`. Added as a
permanent regression assertion in `playwright_smoke.py`.

Also bumped `.mobile-shop-header` (the "OnBrandCraftz" wordmark) from 24px to 30px
and `#home-greeting` from 14px to 16px per Scott's explicit ask, both already
correctly `text-align:center` (confirmed via computed style, not just the CSS
declaration) -- the earlier "not centered" read was almost certainly the header
overflow visually crowding everything else, not a real centering bug.

Full suite (89/89) + 3x clean playwright_smoke.py before shipping.

## 2026-07-30 — Ask/Chat screen UX pass (screen-by-screen audit, page 3, build 044251c-v281)
Third screen in Scott's screen-by-screen UX audit (Login, Home already done). Ask on
mobile and the desktop Command Center are the same screen (`#screen-cmd`) -- plan was
drafted, sent through an adversarial review agent before any code, then approved by
Scott (`chips: hide after first real send`).

1. **Empty-conversation greeting.** `/ws/chat` only sends `{type:'history'}` `if
   history:` (main.py) -- a brand-new session got nothing at all, so `#chat-msgs`
   stayed completely blank below the "Ask Frank" title. Added a client-side-only
   greeting bubble (`_showEmptyChatGreeting()`), fired when the history payload is a
   confirmed-empty array. Worded as a capability intro, not a time-of-day salutation,
   since Home already shows "Good {morning/afternoon/evening}, Scott" and showing that
   twice in two taps would read as broken, not polished.

2. **Quick-reply chips now hide after the first real send.** Added `id="lc-chips"` +
   `_hideChatChips()`, called from two places: the WS history handler when
   `d.messages.length > 0` (a resumed session with real prior turns), and `sendMsg()`
   on every real send. Deliberately NOT keyed off the greeting bubble's presence
   (client-side-only, never persisted) -- the adversarial review flagged that coupling
   as a real bug risk: chips would vanish the instant the greeting renders instead of
   after the user actually engages.

3. **Mobile keyboard could cover the input box.** `#chat-msgs`'s mobile max-height
   used a plain `60vh`, which most mobile browsers do not shrink when the on-screen
   keyboard opens (layout vs. visual viewport) -- on a long conversation this could
   push `#chat-input` off-screen under the keyboard. Switched to `60dvh` (same pattern
   already used for `#stage-wrap`), with the `60vh` declaration left in place
   immediately before it as an automatic fallback for browsers without `dvh` support.

Full suite (89/89) + 3x clean playwright_smoke.py before shipping.

## 2026-07-31 — Approvals screen UX pass (screen-by-screen audit, page 4, build 155c639-v282)
Fourth screen in Scott's screen-by-screen UX audit (Login, Home, Ask/Chat already done).
"Approvals" is the user-facing label for what the code still internally calls the
"Action Center" -- the staged-action approve/reject gate. Plan drafted, sent through an
adversarial review agent before any code, then two remaining decisions approved by
Scott (Today badge should count medium severity too; "Action Center" -> "Approvals"
string cleanup included in this pass).

Unlike Ask/Chat, Approvals is NOT one shared screen definition -- desktop
(`#screen-actions`, `loadActions()`/`renderActionsContent()`) and mobile (`#pp-appr`,
`renderPhoneApprovals()`) are two independent render pipelines sharing some low-level
helpers. That split drove most of the findings below.

1. **Mobile detail-expand.** `renderPhoneApprovals()`'s pcard template had no way to
   expand detail at all -- desktop's `toggleActionDetail()`/`_actionPreviewHtml()`
   (the "why Frank suggested this" reasoning block from the 2026-07-18 audit, plus a
   type-specific preview) were wired into the desktop card template only. Reused both
   functions unmodified, just added a tappable `.pcard-tap` area + `#act-detail-{id}`
   container to the mobile card, same id convention desktop uses.

2. **Confirm-dialog wording.** `_APPROVE_CONFIRM_MSGS` fell through to a generic
   "apply this change to your live Etsy listing" message for `create_listing` (creates
   a brand-new listing, not a change to an existing one), `post_tiktok`, and
   `post_pinterest` (neither is an Etsy listing change at all). Added accurate wording
   for all three.

3. **Mobile list went stale while the tab stayed open.** `renderPhoneApprovals()`
   only fired once on tab-open; the badge count kept updating in the background via
   the always-on `loadQueue()` global loader, so the list could visibly drift out of
   sync with the badge. Added a dedicated 30s interval (mirrors the P1S card's own
   interval added earlier the same day) gated on `#pp-appr`'s `on` class.

4. **Blank detail panel for 6 action types (found during adversarial review, not in
   the original draft).** `_actionPreviewBody()` had zero rendering branch for
   `create_listing`, `post_tiktok`, `post_pinterest`, `update_sku_and_category`,
   `listing_video`, `register_command` -- tapping to expand any of them on desktop
   showed a completely blank panel, worst for `create_listing`, the highest-
   consequence write in the app, whose own staging confirm() promises "you'll review
   it once more." Added real preview branches for all six, plus their missing
   `_ACT_TYPE_GLYPH` entries (previously falling back to a generic ❓).

5. **Today badge undercounted.** `ptab-today-badge`/`home-today-badge` only counted
   `summary.high`, never `summary.medium` -- but `renderPhoneToday()`'s own "Needs
   attention" list already includes both, and every System-health/`data_error` card
   (credential/API failures) is always medium severity. A fresh infra alert could sit
   with zero badge nudge until Scott happened to open Today. Now counts both.

6. **"Action Center" -> "Approvals" string cleanup.** ~8 leftover user-facing strings
   (toasts, the new-listing confirm dialog, link labels, panel copy) still said
   "Action Center" instead of "Approvals" -- internal code comments documenting the
   old name were left as-is (never user-facing).

Explicitly rejected during adversarial review: a "System health" section for mobile
Approvals (my original draft) -- ops_runbook's own 2026-07-03 entry (v109/v110)
already deliberately routes infra alerts to the Today tab instead, specifically to fix
a badge/panel mismatch Scott flagged then. Re-adding it to Approvals would reintroduce
that exact bug. Sort/filter on the pending list, per-item risk badges, and pagination
were all considered and left out -- no evidence of a real problem yet.

New test file `tests/test_approvals_ux_audit.py` (source-substring checks, all six
fixes are pure frontend) + 6 new Playwright assertions in `playwright_smoke.py`
(mobile detail-expand + reason block, the 3 new confirm messages, all 6 preview
branches + glyphs, the Today medium-severity badge). Full suite 90/90, Playwright 3x
clean, build 155c639-v282.

## 2026-07-31 — Today screen UX pass (screen-by-screen audit, page 5, build c11563d-v283)
Fifth screen in Scott's screen-by-screen UX audit (Login, Home, Ask/Chat, Approvals
already done). Today (`renderPhoneToday()`) is mobile-only with no desktop
equivalent at all -- confirmed no `#screen-today`, no desktop nav item, deliberate
per the file's own mobile-only-screen convention. Plan drafted, sent through an
adversarial review agent before any code, then two decisions approved by Scott
(missing-file alert shows "View on Etsy" only, no "Let Frank fix it"; badge scope
limited to "while Today is open" rather than extending the app-wide 30s loop).

1. **Alert `detail` text was fetched but discarded.** `sub:''` was hardcoded for
   every alert-derived Needs Attention card even though the backend's `detail`
   field (e.g. exact steps to rotate a leaked credential) was already in the
   fetched payload. Now threaded through.

2. **The single highest-severity alert type could never be tapped.**
   `product_file_integrity` alerts ("customer might receive nothing") only had
   `listing_id` embedded in the `detail` string, never as a structured field --
   added `listing_id` to the alert dict server-side and copied it through in the
   frontend mapper. Adversarial review caught that the sheet's "Let Frank fix it"
   button (Conversion Doctor -- title/tags/description only) has zero
   relationship to a missing file; per Scott's answer, that button is now
   suppressed for this alert type and only "View on Etsy" shows.

3. **A same-day calendar reminder rendered with a green "all good" dot** inside a
   section titled "Needs attention" -- `sevOf()` fell through `severity:"info"` to
   `'good'`, the same styling as a genuinely positive signal. Now reuses this
   app's existing cyan info convention (`.toast.info`/`.feed-tag.info`) instead of
   inventing a new color.

4. **The 5 Today fetches ran sequentially**, each with its own 15s timeout,
   instead of concurrently. Switched to `Promise.all`, with each fetch keeping its
   own inner try/catch so one slow/failing endpoint can't fail-fast and blank
   fields that would otherwise have loaded fine.

5. **Today never polled while open, and its badge only ever reflected
   `/api/actions`, never `/api/alerts`.** A standing critical alert (credential
   leak, expired refresh token, budget-cap overage) could show a red dot on
   Today's own list with zero badge nudge. Fixed with a 30s active-tab poll
   (mirroring Approvals' 2026-07-30 fix) plus a shared `_alertsCritWarnCount`
   variable that `setActionBadge()` folds into its own `hc` computation --
   adversarial review caught that a one-shot DOM push from `renderPhoneToday()`
   alone would get clobbered back down within moments by the independent 30s
   `loadQueue()` tick's own `setActionBadge()` call; the shared-state approach
   survives any caller. `_alertsCritWarnCount` only counts alert-sourced items
   (tagged `source`) to avoid double-counting recommendations already reflected
   in `_actionsSummary`.

6. **Metrics/Star Seller tiles could silently render a stale cache-fallback
   payload as if it were live**, with the count-up tile animation (its own
   comment calls it "a 'this is live data' cue") actively reinforcing the false
   impression. `_fetch_with_degrade()` already tagged a degraded response
   `stale: true` but had zero frontend consumers (confirmed via full-repo grep)
   and no real timestamp -- added a `stale_as_of` field (the actual cache
   entry's timestamp) so the frontend could reuse the existing `_offlineNote()`
   pattern verbatim instead of inventing new copy, and skips the count-up
   animation on a stale metrics payload.

New test file `tests/test_today_ux_audit.py` (source-substring checks, matching
`test_approvals_ux_audit.py`'s style) + extended `tests/test_products_file_
integrity.py` (listing_id field) + `tests/test_http_routes.py` (stale_as_of
timestamp) + 4 new Playwright assertions (badge shared-state fold-in, Fix-button
suppression, `.palert.info` color). One pre-existing Playwright test (`home-
today-badge should mirror the high-severity today count`) needed a one-line fix
-- it implicitly assumed `_alertsCritWarnCount` was always 0, which broke once
the tour's real Today-tab visit (earlier in the same run) legitimately populated
it from live data; now resets that variable before its own isolated assertion.
Full suite 91/91, Playwright 3x clean, build c11563d-v283.

## 2026-07-31 — Create screen UX pass (screen-by-screen audit, page 6, build ab775bc-v284)
Sixth screen in Scott's screen-by-screen UX audit (Login, Home, Ask/Chat, Approvals,
Today done). Create has already been through multiple redesigns this session (7->9
tile rework, status polling, reference-image library, category-routing fixes, wall-art
vision QA, engine-dropdown fixes) -- research explicitly prioritized confirming what's
already solid over finding new problems, and most of the screen held up on direct code
read. The genuinely open items were narrower than prior screens (3 findings + 1 wording
question, vs. 6 substantive findings each for Approvals/Today). Plan drafted, sent
through an adversarial review agent before any code, then two decisions approved by
Scott (extend vision-QA to BOTH Coloring Pages and Planner covers, not just one;
clean up the engine-dropdown label).

1. **A missing API key was misreported as a transient "try again" error.** The
   listing-photo generator's engine dropdown explicitly promises "Frank tells you if
   one's missing when you generate" -- but `goal_loop.run_until_goal()` catches every
   exception uniformly, so a deterministic `ImageGenError("...API_KEY not set...")`
   fell into the same bucket as a genuine transient Gemini/OpenAI 5xx and rendered as
   "no problem with your file, please try again in a moment." False: retrying with no
   key configured fails identically forever. Added a `config_error` failure_kind,
   keyed off the missing-key error message's unique signature (`"_API_KEY not set"`,
   confirmed to appear in exactly 3 raise sites across the codebase, all and only for
   missing-credential cases) -- no changes to goal_loop.py needed.

2. **Coloring Pages and Digital Planner cover art had no automated art-quality
   check**, unlike Wall Art (which got a real vision-QA + retry pass on 2026-07-30).
   Both were single-shot generate-and-hope calls. Adversarial review corrected my
   original framing (start with the cheaper one, Planner covers) -- Coloring Pages is
   actually the higher-*risk* gap despite generating more images, because
   `tools/post_scheduled_coloring.py` runs it unattended on a 4-day cron with zero
   human review before staging, while Planner covers are rare and Scott-triggered
   either way. Scott approved doing both. Extended
   `goal_loop.run_until_goal()` + `image_gen.verify_original_art()` (same pattern as
   Wall Art) to `generate_coloring_page()` and `_generate_cover_image()`.
   Also added a guard (`image_gen.gemini_key_available()`) applied to all three
   call sites now, including the original Wall Art one: `verify_original_art()` has
   its own GEMINI_API_KEY dependency independent of whichever engine generated the
   image, and without the guard a missing key would masquerade as an ordinary QA
   miss -- retried uselessly with a "fix this" correction the model can't act on,
   then still shipped unverified anyway. Now it's detected up front and skips
   straight to a single generate call with a clear log line, matching each
   function's original single-shot behavior when Gemini isn't configured.

3. **Two small copy/comment fixes**, bundled into this pass: a stale doc comment
   above the `/api/reference-images*` routes still claimed nothing used them for AI
   generation (false since Wall Art's reference-style wiring shipped 2026-07-30,
   comment-only, never user-facing); and the listing-photo engine dropdown's
   "Standard (default · only one with transparent background)" label carried
   leftover boilerplate from a sticker/cut-out context -- this tool never produces a
   transparent background (it composites a real product into a lifestyle scene).

New test files `tests/test_create_screen_audit.py` (missing-key classification via
direct route-handler call + frontend/comment source checks) and
`tests/test_coloring_planner_verify_retry.py` (10 tests mirroring
`test_wall_art_verify_retry.py`'s existing pattern: pass-first-try, retry-once,
exhausted-retries-still-returns-a-file, missing-Gemini-key-skips-QA, and a real
generation failure still returns None/False for both `generate_coloring_page()` and
`_generate_cover_image()`). No new Playwright coverage needed -- this pass is almost
entirely backend logic (error classification, vision-QA), not new interactive UI; the
direct-call and source-substring tests already give stronger coverage than a DOM
check would. Full suite 93/93, Playwright 3x clean, build ab775bc-v284.

`gemini_key_available()` call now actually ran in CI -- and CI has no GEMINI_API_KEY,
so the guard correctly skipped the QA loop, but the test's 3 pre-existing assertions
(retry count, verify call count) assumed the loop always runs. Passed locally only
because a real key happened to be configured in this dev environment, masking the
gap -- classic "works on my machine." Root cause: `test_wall_art_verify_retry.py`
never mocked `gemini_key_available()` at all before this change, since the function
didn't have that dependency until this same pass added it.
Fix: every test in that file now explicitly mocks `gemini_key_available()` (True for
the QA-runs tests, False for a new dedicated skip-QA test), same pattern already used
correctly in the two new test files from this pass. Verified with
`GEMINI_API_KEY`/`GOOGLE_API_KEY` unset locally (matching CI exactly) before
re-pushing -- full suite 93/93, Playwright 3x clean.

## 2026-07-31 — More screen UX pass (screen-by-screen audit, page 7, build 9054fb6-v286)
Seventh screen in Scott's screen-by-screen UX audit (Login, Home, Ask/Chat,
Approvals, Today, Create done). More is the mobile-only launcher menu
(_PHONE_MORE/renderPhoneMore()) -- desktop has no equivalent, its sidebar lists
these 15 destinations as flat nav items directly. Research, plan, adversarial
review, Scott's go-ahead, then implementation -- same pipeline as prior screens.

1. **A prior fix's own stated intent never actually reached mobile.** Commit
   cfb53f8 (2026-07-17) moved Settings out of desktop's "Advanced" sidebar
   section into "Shop" (everyday/non-technical, unlike Tasks/Workflows/
   Security/AI Core/Agents) -- but the ops_runbook entry that commit added
   claimed this covered mobile too ("mobile's More screen reuses the same
   shared .nav-item DOM"), which was never true: _PHONE_MORE was never
   touched. `files` had the identical mismatch (desktop: Shop; mobile:
   Advanced) with no prior fix even claiming otherwise. Moved both to Shop
   in `_PHONE_MORE`, matching desktop.
2. Two label mismatches fixed: "Tools" -> "Tools & Skills", "Brand kit" ->
   "Brand Kit", matching the desktop nav-item and each destination screen's
   own title exactly.
3. **Decorative icon/chevron spans had no aria-hidden**, unlike every
   comparable icon elsewhere in the app since the 2026-07-08 a11y pass --
   `_PHONE_MORE` predates that pass and was missed. Added `aria-hidden="true"`
   to both `.pmi` and `.pmc` spans.
4. Two dead-code cleanups (archived via `tools/trash.py`, not deleted
   outright): a `badge-conversations` DOM lookup with no matching element
   anywhere, and a vestigial `.more-row[data-tier="advanced"]` CSS selector
   that never matched real markup (`_PHONE_MORE` has no tier-gating; the
   real markup is `.pmore-item`/`.pmore-grp`).
5. Self-caught while implementing (not from adversarial review): the
   onboarding tour's own "More" step copy explicitly narrated the OLD
   grouping (Settings alongside Tasks/Calendar under "Advanced") -- would
   have gone stale the moment finding 1 shipped. Fixed the tour body text
   and added a dedicated test assertion for it.
No live badges were added to the launcher itself -- Scott confirmed a
badge-free list is fine, since even desktop's sidebar counts aren't
proactively kept fresh outside the Approvals tab.
New `tests/test_more_screen_audit.py` (6 checks) plus 3 new Playwright
assertions. Full suite + 3x Playwright clean before shipping.


## 2026-07-31 — DP1030 listing photo: text overrun in the GoodNotes how-to graphic, fixed
Scott reported (screenshot of the Products review modal for the ADHD Digital
Planner, DP1030): photo 6 (the 3-panel "HOW TO USE YOUR STICKERS IN GOODNOTES"
graphic) had visibly overlapping/overrunning text between panels, despite the
automated QC sweep reporting a clean "0 FAIL - 0 WARN - 8 PASS" -- a real
CLAUDE.md quality-gate miss (QC only validates file integrity, never the
visual correctness of PIL-composited listing photos).

**Root cause:** `tools/gen_planner_listing_photos.py`'s `make_howto()` split
each step's body text on manually-typed `\n` characters and drew each
resulting line via `ImageDraw.text()` with zero check against the panel's
actual pixel width -- despite an inline comment claiming it was "word-wrapped
manually," which was never true. PIL never wraps text on its own. Step 2's
longer copy ("Open GoodNotes 6 -> tap Elements (diamond) -> Stickers tab ->
tap + -> select all 9 PNG files") ran past the panel edge into the next
panel. `tools/gen_sticker_listing_photos.py`'s `make_howto()` (used for the 6
standalone sticker-pack listings) had the byte-identical defect, not yet
triggered but latent.

Traced which pipeline actually produced DP1030's broken photo: `build_
product.py`'s "Build whole product" flow (the one-tap flow used to originally
build DP1030-1034) calls the older `generate_for_planner()` -> `make_howto()`
path, not the newer AI-photorealistic pipeline added 2026-07-17
(`generate_ai_photos_for_planner()` -> `tools/listing_photo_pipeline.py`,
whose own how-to slot deliberately has zero baked-in text -- "added in Canva
after" per its own scene prompt). Confirms `build_product.py` is still on the
pre-2026-07-17 photo path; worth a separate look at whether it should switch,
flagged to Scott but not changed here (out of scope for this bug report).

**Fix:** added a real `wrap_text(d, text, font, max_width)` helper (measures
actual rendered width via `textbbox`) to both files, applied to both title
and body text with dynamic vertical line stacking so a wrapped title pushes
the body down instead of overlapping it. Verified by rendering both fixed
graphics directly (DP1030's how-to + one sticker pack's how-to) -- clean, no
overrun. Added `tests/test_howto_photo_text_wrap.py`: asserts every wrapped
line fits its panel's actual width across all 5 planners and all 6 sticker
packs, plus explicit '\n' breaks still work and long unbroken lines actually
wrap. DP1030's actual staged photo still needs regenerating (re-run the Build
flow for DP1030) now that the generator is fixed -- the one currently sitting
in the review queue is still the pre-fix version until that happens.
